members.title: 赌石，做珠宝，然后召唤克总？《地渊珠宝匠》新品节试玩现已免费开放

news.body:
伴随着前任主人留下的箴言，维多利亚风格的工作室在地震低鸣中灯影闪烁。你强打精神，拿起手中的工具，瞄准手中灰扑扑的原石，莫名一阵眩晕。那流苏般绚丽的颜色，不该是正常矿石的皮相。但你别无选择，只能探索其背后的真相，哪怕背后的代价是疯狂。
以上，就是入围了2026年indie play最佳设计奖的《地渊珠宝匠》为玩家展示的神秘世界。目前，游戏已参加本次Steam新品节，并开放公开试玩。
《地渊珠宝匠》是一款带有「赌石」元素的工坊经营游戏。玩家将继承地下城市法顿霍姆中的旧珠宝店「朱红馆」，在有限的营业时间里，从挑选原石到切割宝石并设计饰品，凭靠自己的眼力和手艺，完成来客们的各种委托以赚取收益，并让「朱红馆」重回辉煌。
与常见的模拟经营游戏不同，《地渊珠宝匠》在原本就「一刀穷，一刀富」的刺激赌石历程外，还叠加了一丝神秘的克苏鲁元素，为整个游戏的狂热基调降温。
在收购来的质朴原石内，玩家不仅会发现足以让人一夜暴富的完美宝石，也会发现一些难言的诡异物质，而这一切似乎与「朱红馆」的前任主人——主角姐姐的失踪息息相关。
《地渊珠宝匠》在采石的玩法模式中，添加了一条名为「觉知值」的属性。接触特定矿石、切凿异常结晶等一系列操作，都会提高玩家的觉知值。越过临界点后，玩家会发现「朱红馆」内出现的种种离奇异象。这些从矿石中剥离出来的「不该存在之物」，往往既是危险源，也是破局的钥匙。
当然，在克苏鲁的世界，一味索求真相只会引人疯狂。游戏有意地将诡异的节奏放缓，让玩家在有规律的经营日常中，慢慢沉浸入这个虚构的世界。在源源不断的生意中，玩家可以不断积累声誉，升级执照，从而获取更加稀有的矿石。
面对客人们形形色色的委托，玩家要学会用到各种手工道具互相配合，在不伤害宝石的情况下将原石剥落。其中的细节策略，不亚于对这块石头做一次「全面手术」。
在获取到宝石以后，玩家也需要选择合适的切割方法，增加宝石的观赏性，进一步放大宝石的价值。有时候多次的完美打击，甚至会让角色进入心流，创造出超越完美的作品。
这些打磨精致的耀眼珍品，除了直接交付给收藏家之外，也可以被制作成不同款式的精致饰品。
无论是放到拍卖会售卖攫取收益，亦或是放在陈列室展出提高名誉，还是待在自己手上增加种种奇妙异能，全部交给玩家自己来选择。
现在，准备好了吗？如果你也希望在雕琢中寻找完美，在日常中体验异象，不妨现在就参与《地渊珠宝匠》的公开试玩，一起踏入《地渊珠宝匠》那神秘而璀璨的古老纪元。

news.body:
由新西兰开发商 Digital Confectioners 打造的《龙骨海盗》（Keelblade）是一款支持1—6名玩家游玩的奇幻海盗动作角色扮演游戏。游戏现已在 Steam 推出首个公开试玩版，同时为迎接中国玩家，所有游戏内文字与字幕均已加入简体中文支持。
《龙骨海盗》免费试玩版现已上线，立即下载，扬帆启航！试玩版将在北京时间10月20日至27日举行的 Steam 新品节期间持续开放。
你的船不仅是交通工具，更是由你亲手建造、自由定制，并在整个冒险旅程中始终相伴的家园。在自己的海盗船上建造设施，随后掌舵起航，探索广阔的开放式奇幻世界。形形色色的奇异岛屿散布其中，越是深入探索，面临的危险也越大。
《龙骨海盗》的战斗考验玩家对时机的把握、策略运用与操作技巧。熟悉敌人的攻击模式，合理管理精力，通过闪避、破防与精准弹反应对攻势。搭配不同武器、天赋与强力魔法，打造属于自己的独特战斗风格。
世界各地潜伏着怪物与传说中的强大首领，考验着玩家的出手时机、站位与战前准备。与船员协同搭配武器和能力，寻找破绽，在惊险的首领战中赢得胜利。
部分首领还可在难度更高的“挑战模式”条件下再次挑战，供渴望更艰难战斗的船员一试身手。
每一次出航探索都伴随着新的危险与收获。在岛屿上搜寻隐藏的宝藏，发现新的制作配方，再将战利品带回船上，用于升级船只与角色装备。
你可以独自挑战危机四伏的岛屿，也可以通过在线合作，与最多五名好友组成六人海盗船队。协调彼此的装备配置、共享资源，携手攻克重重挑战。

members.title: 《中世纪崛起》（Medieval Ascendant）参展 Steam 新品节，免费试玩版10月19日至26日开放

news.body:
2026年10月，独立游戏工作室 netplay entertainment 今日宣布，旗下深度中世纪人生与家族王朝模拟游戏《中世纪崛起》（Medieval Ascendant）将参加10月19日至26日举行的 Steam 新品节。游戏免费试玩版即日起在 Steam 商店页面开放下载，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux，并将在新品节期间持续开放。针对中国市场，游戏同时公布官方简体中文名《中世纪崛起》，并推出全新本地化的主视觉与商店封面图。
代代相传，书写你的家族史诗
在《中世纪崛起》中，玩家将来到奇幻王国奥尔德雷德，直面残酷的中世纪世界。你最初只是一名身无分文的农奴，要在等级森严的社会中一步步往上爬。角色离世后，继承人会接过你留下的一切，每一代人的选择都将决定家族的兴衰。
种田、学手艺，或者垄断市场，在五个各具特色的行省里建立庞大的生产网络。你可以凭经济实力、公开开战或暗中密谋来左右王国局势。最终是靠铁血征伐、权谋算计，还是金钱的力量登上权力顶峰，全看你自己。
游戏特色
· 真正的王朝模拟：历经数代人，从毫无权利的农奴一路攀升至贵族高位。游戏包含遗传、继承与教育系统，还能通过联姻和嫁妆结成战略同盟。
· 动态经济系统：五个行省各有本地市场，需求随人口变化，还有 NPC 竞争对手和季节波动。干旱、瘟疫和战争都会影响物价，你可以用经济手段让一个行省繁荣兴旺，也能让它陷入饥荒。
· 完整的生产链：游戏中的所有商品都可以自己生产，不同行省在特定商品上各有优势。
· 战略开战，战术对决：与敌对家族开战，或抵御邻国入侵、保卫王国。每场战斗分多个回合进行，角色可能落下永久伤残，甚至战死沙场。
· 死亡不是终点：家族传承代代延续，每一局都会生成独一无二的故事，对话走向难以预料。
关于试玩版
Steam 新品节免费试玩版包含《中世纪崛起》完整的开局内容，支持 Windows、macOS 和 Linux。玩家将以农奴身份迈出崛起的第一步：从下地干活、学习手艺，到赚到第一笔真正能带来影响力的钱。
netplay entertainment 创始人 Robert Kolloch 表示：“《中世纪崛起》讲的是一场长线博弈：一个人的一生能带来怎样的改变，一个家族经过几代人又能走到哪一步。新品节试玩版是开启这段旅程的最好机会。我们也很高兴能用专属的中文名和美术，把这款游戏带给中国玩家。”

news.body:
LEGO & Netflix Presented a Giant Figure of Derpy Tiger from KPop Demon Hunters
The massive LEGO statue is roughly half the size of its creator, LEGO designer Björn Ramant.
Björn Ramant
A giant LEGO statue of Derpy Tiger from KPop Demon Hunters became Netflix and LEGO's most recent collaborative project. The huge figure is about half the size of the creator behind it, LEGO designer Björn Ramant.
The massive LEGO-made Derpy Tiger took about 2.5 months to create, from sketching out the design to assembling the final pieces, the creator shared on his socials. It required 4 metal beams for additional support, since the figure was so heavy. Ramant revealed that he used around 37,000 pieces to build Derpy Tiger. Considering that an average 2x4 LEGO brick weighs approximately 2.5 grams (0.088 ounces), it weighs about 92,500 grams or 3,256 ounces.
Right now, the giant LEGO Derpy is on display at LEGO World 2026 in Utrecht. There is much more to see there for pop culture fans. The figures displayed at this year's event include the 1989 Batmobile, One Piece Whale, and a life-sized Toy Story's Woody.
Before rediscovering his passion for LEGO in 2016, Ramant was a Software Architect. In 2020, he competed in LEGO Masters, and in 2021, he started his part-time business designing and building LEGO figures. If you want to see more of Ramant's LEGO creations, check them out on his Instagram.

news.title: 让游戏性发生质变，“肉鸽+X”是怎么实现的？
news.summary_raw: 以独游ForgeTax为核心案例，解析“肉鸽+装备强化”的玩法融合逻辑与现存不足，探讨局内Build对游戏性的提升作用及跨品类应用。

members.title: 让游戏性发生质变，“肉鸽+X”是怎么实现的？

news.body:
这一锤下去，会很疯狂
一把原本价值360G的旧剑，在我的巧妙锻造下，价值一路飙升到了几百、上千亿。数值爆炸式增长带来的即时反馈，再加上锻造过程中需要频繁要做出的高风险抉择，可以说，ForgeTax让我彻底玩上头了。
玩过DNF的玩家，或许会对这套框架相当熟悉，没错，其核心玩法其实就是强化装备的底色，作为一款小体量独游，ForgeTax把背景故事和玩法逻辑做得相当简单，基于暗黑风格下，游戏包装了一个与邪神达成21天契约的故事，邪神每天会发放3把旧剑，玩家需要做的是进行加热锻造，并上交足额价值的剑，在21天内生存下来（21天之后还可选择延长契约，挑战无尽模式）。
当然，并不是每把剑都能锻造出上述的高价值，锻造的过程中往往伴随着高风险和高收益，随着强化等级的增加，锻造失败的概率也在同步增加。不过，如果只是停留在概率层面上，那么游戏也仅限于一个装备强化模拟器，谈不上让人上头可言。事实上，ForgeTax加入了一套完整的肉鸽框架，巧妙串联起整个进程，让游戏性发生了意想不到的变化。
肉鸽+装备强化=？
ForgeTax的底层框架是一套标准的Roguelike，它拥有单局制、永久死亡、局内Build等核心特点，在具体聊游戏玩法之前，我想有必要先简单分析一下强化装备自带的吸引力。
在不少MMORPG游戏里，游戏通过强化成功概率的宏观调控，以及强化成功后带来的属性提升，借由强化装备回收大量资源，维持着游戏经济系统的健康运转，与此同时，强化过程中伴随的高风险和高收益，也让无数玩家趋之若鹜。
强化装备最根本的吸引力，在于它完美运用了心理学中最有效的行为强化模式「可变比率强化」，具体来说，奖励在不确定的次数后出现，但平均频率是固定的，连续失败后下一次成功的概率会逐步提升，而当低概率事件意外成功时，大脑会瞬间产生巨大的多巴胺释放，带来强烈的爽感。
ForgeTax复刻了这套强化逻辑，强化过程中会出现5个概率事件“破坏、损伤、维持、成功、大成功”，顾名思义，触发破坏事件时，装备会被损坏；触发损伤事件，强化等级-1，装备价值相应减少；触发维持事件时，装备不变；触发成功事件时，强化等级提升，装备价值提升1.5倍；触发大成功事件，强化等级提升，装备价值提升3.5倍。
而随着强化等级的提升，破坏和损伤事件的权重又会不断增加，到了强化+20以上，破坏的概率超过60%。不过，在经过10次锻造后，玩家能够获得短暂的奖励时间「入神」，在「入神」期间，装备不会被破坏，玩家要做的事就是尽可能砸出更多锤，让剑在这一期间尽可能强化到更高等级。
依个人数十小时的体验来看，「入神」也是游戏里正反馈的主要来源，原本价值数万的装备，在此期间或许能翻上数千万倍，几秒内实现暴富，极大增加了玩家的心流体验。
看到这里你或许不难发现，如果仅靠强化的玩法框架，那么游戏的负反馈会远大于正反馈，前面辛辛苦苦砸到高额价值的剑在后期毁于一旦，从心理学的角度来看，这种失去的痛苦远大于获得的快乐。
由此，ForgeTax自然需要更多变量，去影响强化的结果，简单来说，就是让强化最终的成功概率更趋于玩家心中的理想值，合理拉升正反馈循环。基于此，「遗物」的加入，在实现这一目的的同时，也带来了更多可玩性和深度。
关于「遗物」的设计，ForgeTax引入了两个关键的物品变量：一是锻造所需要的剑，二是剑上贡之后得到的钱。剑是用来兑换遗物的主要道具，而钱则可以用来刷新遗物商店，回合内刷新所需的钱会随着回合数以及刷新次数递增。可以说，「遗物」的加入，既让玩家在剑的消耗层面上多了一份考量，又让钱有了一个稳定的消耗渠道。
「遗物」大致可以分为3种类型。一是提升剑的价值，游戏里剑的价值计算方式是“强化倍率x基础价值”，强化最高30级，比如说黄金齿轮的效果“每3次成功或大成功，剑价值+15%”，假设在强化过程中成功30次，算上成功/大成功本身的倍数，以及强化等级30的倍率，最终价值至少翻上千万倍。
要知道，这还只是单个遗物的效果，游戏里一共能装备8个遗物，在各个遗物的互相加成下，剑在强化过程中的价值最终成几何倍增长，带来了超高密度的心流体验。
二是提高强化等级和强化保护。前面提到过，强化等级越高，成功概率越低，如果按正常情况下，装备强化几乎不可能达到+30。由此，游戏内设计了不少提供强化保护的遗物，比如说将每把剑首次破坏变成损伤；将破坏变成损失，但剑价值减半等等。
三是辅助效果。比如说直接增加「入神」时间、增加商人栏位、加快锻造速度、让发放的剑直接从+7开始等等类型的遗物。这些遗物单看可能毫无特点，但与其他遗物组合起来，能够形成 1+1＞2 的联动效应。
以个人玩的流派为例，我分别选择了“入神时间持续时间+2秒”、“入神期间每次锻造速度提升10%，最高叠加到60%”、“入神期间大成功签+6”、“每次维持，剑价值+12%”、“每3次成功或大成功，剑价值+15%”、“强化达到+7时，每次成功或大成功，剑价值+15%”、“每2次成功，额外强化+1”、“每把剑首次破坏变成损伤”这8个遗物。
仅看词条，或许你会感受到这套遗物能够产生不错的联动效应，接下来请看实际效果：
这把原本+7、价值1W的旧剑，仅靠一次入神价值便翻了整整15W倍，最后变成了+27、价值15亿的「魔剑：屠龙者」。这自然得益于遗物的联动效应：入神时间加上锻造速度，让我在期间出锤的次数几乎多了两倍，而入神期间大成功概率提升，联动上其他三条成功加强化等级和价值的遗物，也让剑的强化等级和价值完成了质的飞跃。
外加上每隔2天会出现的商人，能够用钱买到一些关键道具，比如说保护装备不被损坏的龙鳞，能够让失败结果进行回溯的发条，直接增加入神进度的星星等等，在道具和遗物的效果加持下，游戏大幅降低了强化装备失败后带来的挫败感。
当然，如果只是将通关定义在前21天，那么「遗物」的Build作用几乎可以忽略，游戏在前21天并没有设置太高的门槛，甚至说不需要花费太多心思，就可以轻松完成。但想要生存50、100天，那么就需要合理规划遗物，尤其到了后期，即便搭配了完美的遗物，仍然需要打造出几把甚至十几把高价值剑才能够完成上贡任务。
进一步来看，无论是「遗物」还是商人，其实都在一定程度上改变了强化的底层逻辑，单次强化的结果随机性在其影响下变得更小，如果说强化仅能在前1小时提供乐趣，那么局内Build则让游戏有了几小时、甚至数十小时体验的潜力。
或许是个好创意，但还不够
需要指出的是，ForgeTax仍存在不少痛点。
肉鸽的Build元素的确放大了其玩法乐趣，但这还不足以让它具备可复玩性和再开一把的理由，在我看来，ForgeTax的Build深度远远不够。
一方面，遗物之间虽有联动，但尚未形成明确的流派，并且没有按阶段不断解锁新遗物，成长曲线相对较平，这也导致了游戏在各个阶段的体验几乎一致，没有发生太多差异和变化，缺乏了刷新到高级遗物产生质变的爽感，玩到后面实属无聊。
另一方面，作为肉鸽游戏，ForgeTax的Build广度太过单一，它完全具备着往多维度发展的可能。设想一下，游戏完全可以加入不同职业，并根据职业进一步区分专属的遗物和技能效果，从而往更体系化的流派方向发展；再比如说在局外重新构建出一套养成体系，绑定单局收益，使其转化为局外成长。成熟的肉鸽游戏的核心在于让玩家经常失败，但每次失败都更想再来一次，但很显然，ForgeTax并没有做到这点。
再者，ForgeTax在打造出高价值的装备也缺乏了相应的反馈，游戏里虽然有做了装备图鉴，让每把剑有着不同的成长路径，但其达成条件过于简单，玩上一小时基本能够解锁全图鉴，不足以驱动玩家反复游玩。这其实也是独游的局限性，在MMO里打造出高价值的装备，得到了属性的提升的同时，也收获了来自其它玩家的反馈，某种意义来说，它还兼具社交的价值，这种情绪驱动也赋予了强化装备更强烈的正反馈。
不过，即便是还不够完美，但ForgeTax还是让我们看到了肉鸽的Build元素在和强化装备结合后迸发出的游戏性，原本平平无奇的装备强化玩法，在加入局内Build之后，的确有了更多可能性。
此外，ForgeTax所释放的乐趣，其实再次也说明了局内Build的魅力。在我看来，局内Build的魅力，核心在于它把随机性从一种干扰的定位，变成了每局重新生成的内容，同时又让局内成长从线性数值变成了玩家一步步做出来的策略选择，放大了流派成型后的成就感和爽感。
而局内Build的开发成本也相对较低，开发者只需设计出几十上百个基础模块，便能让玩家组合出成千上万种组合，不同模块之间往往能迸发出很多意想不到的化学反应。不难发现，局内Build的设计思路，近年来越来越经常在其他品类里见到了。
将局内Build融合得最最成功的产品或许是《英雄联盟》，「海克斯大乱斗」通过加入强化符文，让游戏可玩性和乐趣发生质变。强化符文的随机性，让游戏每局都充满了可能性，而不同符文的组合配合上英雄的技能特性，又迸发出了巧妙的化学反应，不仅极大程度地弥补了英雄短板，同时也弥补了玩家的操作差距。
比如说“回归基本功”，以封印大招的代价，换取伤害、治疗、护盾、技能急速等收益，相当适配瑞兹、盖伦这类不依赖大招的英雄。而当Build成型，触发各种增益效果、打出爆炸伤害时，爽感甚至比胜利还要来得强烈。不仅如此，在强化符文的随机性下，玩家往往会将失败原因归咎于运气不好，有效降低了失败带来的负反馈。
基于这种极强的正反馈下，或许也解释了为何「海克斯大乱斗」让人如此上头，肉鸽局内BD元素与MOBA局内自带的成长路径进行深度融合后，原本已经固化的装备、打法被再次重组，在原有基础上碰撞出了更新鲜、更富有想象力的玩法。
当然，这并不是设计师拍拍脑袋做出来的玩法融合，恰恰相反，融合局内Build是《英雄联盟》经过长时间反复验证和实践的成果。比「海克斯大乱斗」更早出现局内Build的是「斗魂竞技场」以及「云顶之弈」，「云顶之弈」自S6双城之战赛季中加入强化符文后，便将此机制保留至今，从结果看来，强化符文也帮助「云顶之弈」打破了自走棋原本玩法固化、公式化的局限性。
个人认为，对于自走棋这类策略性较强的品类而言，随机性的合理加入，在既不损害游戏原有策略深度的同时，也增加了更多维度上的策略考量，这份随机性也使得游戏常玩常新，让玩家在几百、上千局的体验中始终保持新鲜感和期待。
局内Build在我看来不失为一种万能公式，它能够适配绝大部分自带成长和养成属性的玩法，并且能够在很大程度上削弱数值的影响力和权重。从体验上看，它同时提供掌控感与惊喜感，让玩家在不确定中寻找确定，形成“成型时爽，失败时再来一次”的心流循环；从重复游玩上看，每局独立成型、套路难以固化，既压缩了成长曲线，也延长了玩法的体验周期，它更像是一种玩法设计里的万能公式，能够赋予玩法全新的定义。
结语
再回到ForgeTax本身。
从销量以及玩家的反馈看，ForgeTax做得并不算成功。它是一款创意鲜明但体验略显极端的游戏，聚焦于单把剑的强化结果是否达到预期的玩家，很容易在前几分钟内被劝退，很难沉淀到游戏的核心玩法循环里。
只有当玩家不再只盯着这一锤有没有成功，而是开始盘算遗物怎么搭配才能收益最大化、怎么将剑的利用率达到最高时，ForgeTax玩法的核心魅力才真正开始。

news.title: 为什么原神和绝区零都是三渲二，很多人却觉得三渲二游戏消失了？
news.summary_raw: 梳理三渲二技术的发展脉络，解释原神、绝区零等作品虽采用三渲二，但因风格演变、中间层项目消失，使大众产生三渲二游戏变少的错觉。

members.title: 为什么原神和绝区零都是三渲二，很多人却觉得三渲二游戏消失了？

news.body:
作者：叶兰舟 首发公众号：叶师傅说游戏
广义上说，所有基于3D 模型制作，但目标是仿 2D 手绘效果的，都可以被称为三渲二，它们统统都属于NPR（非真实感渲染）的行列。
可是那种看起来像老动画的三渲二，现在确实越来越少了，这又是为什么呢？
我先卖个关子，咱们先从 2000 年开始讲起。
那时候世嘉在Dreamcast 上出了个游戏叫《Jet Set Radio》的，玩法就是一群轮滑少年在东京街头喷漆涂鸦，它通常被认为是首款商业发行的实时赛璐珞渲染作品，当年在东京电玩展一公布就震惊全场。
从这个时候开始，业内对三渲二的共识也逐渐形成了，基本就三点：
第一，轮廓描个黑边，这个非常好理解。
第二，色块化的硬边界阴影。
第三，赛璐璐风格的平涂化色彩处理。
对于做过游戏或者稍有接触的朋友，可能会觉得，听着不难啊？现在到处都有教程，实现起来不是很容易么？
并不是的。
要「做出来」，现在确实不难，但要「做得好」，可一点也不简单了。
一般搞写实的 3D 画面，现代游戏用的都是 PBR 流程，它是基于物理学的，计算机模拟出物体的材质怎么反光、怎么透光，引擎计算好光线，往上一照，效果就出来了。
这个过程本质上繁琐得很，但已经被现代工具包装得非常好，以至于像我这样图形学的外行人也能试着玩玩。比如你看下面这两张图，都是我游戏里用的素材：
这两张图，模型没有半点区别，纯粹就是烘焙了一遍光影和材质，画面效果就天差地别，从「这是什么鬼」，达到了「作为低成本独游似乎还可以接受嘛」的程度。
这跟我个人的本事没有半毛钱关系，纯粹是计算机图形学几十年来的积累和红利，我只要改几个参数，点一下烘焙就完了，不太费事儿。
而三渲二呢，完全不是一回事，它追求的就不是现实。
现实里的物体有黑边吗？现实里的阴影通常也不是连续渐变的吧？
那么原教旨主义的三渲二，就很多管线都得自己搞，更何况 2000 年那时候还远没现在这么多方便的技术和技巧，而这也让它的进步相当缓慢。
在很长一段时间里，它都是只能远观，不能近看的。
制作方法一般是把模型整体放大一圈，背面涂黑，这样可以自动生成一圈粗细均匀的黑线，然后加上平涂效果，好处是制作很简单，坏处是基本只能看个氛围，一拉进就没法看了。
直到14 年的时候，日本小厂 Arc System Works，ASW——其实可以叫他们三渲二仙人——才把这门技艺推动了一个新的境界。
2014 年，他们的《罪恶装备 Xrd》上市，格斗玩家集体看傻了，卧槽，这个三渲二看着好像不太一样啊？这个精细度跟以前的简直完全不同哇！
这个核心就在他们的首席数字美术师本村・C・纯也身上。他搞出了一套独门方法，圈内叫「本村线」。
他用的办法，简单概括一下，就是手调仙人。
首先，描边要手调。
统一生成的黑边没法细看，颧骨和下巴这种地方要更粗，脸颊等该细的地方细，这种只能手调。
然后，内部线条也手调。
比如上图那些肌肉和衣褶，常规做法是在贴图上直接手绘画出黑线，但这样的话，由于分辨率是固定的，镜头一拉近，手绘上去的斜向黑线立即就会出现锯齿。
所以本村的做法，就是先弄一张特殊的源贴图，这贴图只有一组规整的、互相平行的黑色直线条纹，然后让美术手动调整模型每一个面的 UV，把原本平直的条纹，通过 UV 的拉伸和扭转，贴到角色的曲面上。
如果你没看懂的话，只要知道这里需要巨量的人工就行了……
阴影也一样。
一个高面数的角色模型，上面会有很多细碎的褶皱和肌肉的起伏，如果直接使用卡通着色，那么这些褶皱上细小的凹凸，就会变成大量细碎的小阴影，让身上显得很脏。
但日式赛璐珞手绘动画恰恰不能要这个——众所周知，日式的手绘动画，都要主动概括形体，只画大块的阴影，刻意忽略皮肤上、衣服上微小起伏带来的细碎阴影。
所以本村的办法是什么呢？依然是手调……
好吧，你可以想象一下这里的人工有多大的量了。这个真的不是一般游戏公司会轻易去做的。
当然效果也确实是好。
后来 2018 年的《龙珠斗士 Z》，就是用这套东西把悟空做成了「能动的鸟山明原画」，被称为史上还原度最高的龙珠游戏。
这根本不是「搞个滤镜」就能解决的问题，而是需要技术美术人肉堆出来的，真正的手工仙人。
也正因为这样，就跟劳斯莱斯标榜自己纯手工一样，在 2010-2016 年那个时代，三渲二是稀缺品，是正经能写进宣发里的差异化卖点，漫改游戏就大量使用这种技术，
CC2 这家公司靠这门手艺接下了大量的漫改订单，从火影到JoJo，漫改格斗十有八九是三渲二。
然后 2020 年，《原神》来了……
它把三渲二从「一门独家手艺」，变成了「一套被验证成功的工业化标准」。
从角色着色到面部法线，从描边到昼夜变化下的卡通光照，米哈游把整条管线的工业化生产打通了，还在全球市场赚了大钱，这一下子就还带出了幻塔，异环，无限暖暖这种工业化的二游，大家统统用的都是三渲二NPR，既有科技又有狠活。
这就像以前大家在家里做炸鸡，得腌制、调料，折腾半天，然后转头一看肯德基麦当劳出来了一样……
纯粹的手工三渲二仙人，就是被工业化挤兑的小店。
那问题又来了，这种工业化的场景，跟手工仙人，最大的区别是哪里呢？又为什么会有这样的区别呢？
答案就是开放世界的场景处理。
你回头看 ASW 那些手工仙人的作品，会发现他们的场景其实也是赛璐璐的，角色和背景都是一种风格，像究极风暴就是这样的。
对于这些游戏，场景并不复杂，镜头也多半不是完全自由移动的（比如格斗游戏就只有一个侧面镜头，漫改游戏的镜头跟着演出走）哪些面要描边，要特殊处理，美术的工作量是可预期的。
可工业化二游要做的是什么？开放世界，自由视角啊！！
你让这么大一个能随便转的场景也走纯赛璐璐，每栋楼、每块石头、每棵树都手调法线、手调描边？！
角色已经已经要把 TA 们调吐血了，场景的资产量是角色的几百倍，这个钱谁烧得起？
工业化管线最后给出的答案就是折中：角色继续 NPR，场景改走 PBR 写实，两条腿各走各的。
为了让两种质感别打架，它的过场动画都是各种手绘 2D 、Q 版形象，搞各种漫画风格的特效，来冲淡场景的写实感。
原神则还是往回倒腾了一点，虽然场景本身是 PBR，但美术通过手绘贴图、统一色调，以及压低材质反射的方式，对场景做了二次元化风格修饰，所以写实感不会特别强。
那是不是大家都认命了，用这种法子呢？
倒也不是。
比如手工仙人 ASW，他们的做法是连角色一起写实化，不再是手绘动画的路数了。
再或者是跟米哈游的Varsapura一样，全面拥抱虚幻 5 的写实管线。
而异环、鸣潮、绝区零这些，就还是留在 NPR 里继续堆精度，什么立体渐变的睫毛，虹膜的建模，眼睑的勾线，腮红、唇彩、玉足上的青筋，这些都一点点堆出来。
不过这些的核心都是一样的：真实的材质和光影，以及电影化的运镜变得越来越多，纯粹的赛璐璐色块越来越少，唯一的分歧，只剩「二次元脸」这最后一道防线——是的，所以你才会产生三渲二不见了的错觉。
那三渲二是不是就剩运营二游这一种活法了？也不是，2024 年还出了好几个漂亮的单机。
Cygames 磨了快十年的《碧蓝幻想 Relink》，cel-shading 加上手绘感的横向阴影线，很有老时代三渲二的感觉。
Atlus 同年的《暗喻幻想：ReFantazio》，也是一套高度风格化的卡通渲染，怪诞又高级。
真正消失的，是「中间层」。
现在的三渲二项目基本上就是两种极端。
一种是米哈游，库洛，完美世界这种巨头，在卷工业化和精度。
一种是Atlus、Cygames 这种美术风格高度统一、靠强风格吃饭的单机厂。
夹在中间的那些项目，预算几千万，想做个二游，但又没有自研管线能力的中型团队，做出来的东西既卷不过大厂的精细度，有没有单机厂的强烈风格，在商业上几乎没有活路。
今天的各种卡通渲染材质包也是一键调用，随意做出原神式的着色，AI 生成的贴图几秒钟一张，就让这种「平庸的三渲二」彻底不值钱了 。
这也是你印象中的那些三渲二游戏之所以越来越少的原因。

news.what: 作者叶兰舟梳理三渲二从《Jet Set Radio》到《罪恶装备 Xrd》手工调描边、UV与阴影的做法，再谈《原神》将角色NPR与场景PBR结合的工业化路线，认为消失的是缺乏风格与管线能力的中型项目。

news.title: RocketWerkz' C# framework 'BRUTAL' is now available to all developers
news.summary_raw: Developers who want to complete control over their game's code have a new framework to lean on.

members.title: RocketWerkz' C# framework 'BRUTAL' is now available to all developers

news.body:
RocketWerkz' C# framework 'BRUTAL' is now available to all developers
Developers who want to complete control over their game's code have a new framework to lean on.
Kitten Space Agency and Icarus developer RocketWerkz and game platform operator Ahwoo—both founded by veteran DayZ developer Dean Hall—have announced the open source release of the game development framework known as "BRUTAL," a C#-based framework that offers developers another alternative to third-party game engines like Unity, Unreal Engine, or even Godot.
The framework combines C# and .NET with C++ libraries and low-level graphics access, acting as a foundation for developers to build and maintain their own development tools.
Such options have become more attractive after major debacles like the Unity Runtime Fee saga and Epic Games' announcement that it would be depreciating Unreal's Blueprints function have given some developers cause for concern about the stability of their tech stacks. RocketWerkz has been personally using BRUTAL in the development of Kitten Space Agency, but developers looking for an external case study should check out the most recent update to Ludeon Studios' Rimworld. The developer announced last week that it had ported the game off of Unity onto a new game engine called "Waylith," which it says offers players better performance and a faster start-up time than seen in previous versions.
The framework is free to use in commercial games with no royalty requirements, though the open source license does require developers to provide attribution and display a logo before gameplay when players load your game.
Developers should know that adopting BRUTAL won't be as simple as picking up other beloved open-source engines like Godot. BRUTAL is a programming framework that can be a foundation for proprietary game engines or simply a means to make your game from scratch—a more challenging feat that requires a willingness to embrace the nuts and bolts of a programming language like C#.
In 2025, Hall and Kerbal Space Program creator Felipe Falanghe explained to Game Developer that they found working with BRUTAL to be much easier thanks to advancements in large language models (LLMs). The AI tools allowed Hall, Falaghe, and their colleagues to ask questions about C# libraries and Vulkan documentation, which are both "highly structured, with very clear syntax."
"An LLM is essentially tokenizing language, then putting masses of vectors around that to build linkages between those tokens," Hall said at the time. "What could be better than a highly-structured, in fact brutally structured language?"
The pair said this process was not the same as "vibe-coding," which automatically generates code based on user prompts.
Will more developers make their own game engines?
Ludeon Studios' decision to port Rimworld off of Unity and onto a custom engine powered by BRUTAL also serves as a case study for Hall's belief that programming frameworks, rather than third-party engines, are the future of game development. Reliance on third-party engines has long been a bugbear for Hall, who called out Unity in 2025 for allegedly threatening to terminate Rocketwerkz' license over what he said were false accusations of violating its terms of service.
"You are only as independent as your tools are," he said in a statement accompanying the announcement, saying that while not every developer should have to make their own game engine, every developer should have "the option to do so."
This notion has certainly struck a chord with developers like Mega Crit in the last few years, which switched from Unity to Godot while making Slay the Spire, and barely lost any development time in the process.
Still, don't expect BRUTAL to become the definitive framework for game development anytime soon. Hall told Game Developer last year that he'd prefer it if other developers created their own "simpler" frameworks following a similar approach, rather than trying to turn the open source framework into an industry standard.
"BRUTAL was made to deliver a very specific, kind of hard-to-make game where you need to sit down and ask a whole bunch of questions [about how it works]," he said—an approach that some developers will certainly welcome with open arms. Others will understandably tap out of such a daunting task.

news.title: PEGI begins moving existing digital-only games with loot boxes up to a 16 rating
news.summary_raw: Existing digital-only games that include paid random items, such as loot boxes, are being re-rated PEGI 16 if they currently carry a PEGI 3, 7, or 12 rating.

members.title: PEGI begins moving existing digital-only games with loot boxes up to a 16 rating

news.body:
PEGI begins moving existing digital-only games with loot boxes up to a 16 rating
Games currently rated PEGI 3, 7, or 12 are affected, with updates rolling out through October
Existing digital-only games that include paid random items, such as loot boxes, are being re-rated PEGI 16 if they currently carry a PEGI 3, 7, or 12 rating.
Games Rating Authority policy manager Connor Hinde said in a LinkedIn post that the GRA, which administers PEGI in the UK, started applying the updated criteria to a selection of existing digital games last week.
The new rating is labeled PEGI 16 - Paid random items. It applies whether a game was originally rated through PEGI's Classic procedure or the International Age Rating Coalition (IARC) system.
The changes will continue to roll out progressively through October. The GRA acknowledged that a large number of ratings will change in a short space of time, and directed publishers and developers with questions to the PEGI Helpdesk.
In March, the Entertainment Software Rating Board (ESRB) said it would not be adopting the age-rating changes announced by Pan-European Game Information (PEGI) as it "could be confusing" for users.

news.title: Moonlighter developer delays public playtest of next game over concerns of AI cloning
news.summary_raw: Digital Sun Games is narrowing its early testing of ReVamp to its Discord community following fears of generative AI-enabled cloning.

members.title: Moonlighter developer delays public playtest of next game over concerns of AI cloning

news.body:
Moonlighter developer delays public playtest of next game over concerns of AI cloning
Digital Sun Games is narrowing its early testing of ReVamp to its Discord community following fears of generative AI-enabled cloning.
A recent burst of generative AI-enabled game cloning is forcing established game studios to adjust their development strategies—and in one notable indie studio's case, it means scaling back a previously-planned public playtest for fear of being beat to market by vibe-coding copycats.
Said indie studio is Digital Sun Games, best known for Moonlighter and Moonlighter 2: The Endless Vault. The company is working on an upcoming "Tower Defensevania" game called ReVamp, and had announced plans earlier this month to host a public playtest to solicit player feedback, gather metrics, and improve the upcoming game.
Now however, those plans are on ice. In a post on Steam and Bluesky, the studio informed players that the team is "concerned by recent news of games being reverse-engineered, cloned, and published before the original is even out." (via Kotaku.)
"With launch still months away, a large public build of ReVamp felt like too big a risk," the company said. It will run a "more contained" playtest through its Discord server starting on October 29.
Digital Sun isn't the only studio to cancel promotional plans for fear of AI cloning. Just yesterday, Alliance Arts and Who's You canceled the Steam Next Fest demo for the upcoming game Drunken Goddess Reflux.
Fast-follow video game clones aren't a new phenomenon. Veteran game industry professionals will recall how Vlambeer's Ridiculous Fishing and Asher Vollmer, Greg Wohlwend, and BigGiantCircles' Threes! were rapidly copied on mobile platforms as early as 2013. But indie developers on watering holes on platforms like Reddit have spent the last month describing how scurrilous developers have fed demos, trailers, and images of their games into generative AI tools and quickly rebuilt their basic features from the ground up.
This has all been made possible by longstanding limited copyright protections for video game mechanics and advancements in certain LLMs like Anthropic's Claude and OpenAI's ChatGPT. Said tools have also been recently deployed to decompile older games, driving a new burst of vibe-coded mods.
Digital Sun Studios' announcement highlights how these predatory cloning practices risk harming the market potential for smaller studios looking to break out and build an audience—and how it may require platform owners like Steam to set new policies that disincentivize this behavior. "Showing games early is how indies get seen and find the fans who keep us going," the company wrote. "We hope platforms keep strengthening protections for original work."

news.title: Get Six Awesome PC Games for $9.99 With the gamescom asia Bundle
news.summary_raw: The limited-time collection brings together GigaBash, HELLCARD, Gordian Quest, Winion Virus, Monstrum, and UNYIELDER while supporting Stand Up To Cancer.

members.title: Get Six Awesome PC Games for $9.99 With the gamescom asia Bundle

news.body:
Get Six Awesome PC Games for $9.99 With the gamescom asia Bundle
The limited-time collection brings together GigaBash, HELLCARD, Gordian Quest, Winion Virus, Monstrum, and UNYIELDER while supporting Stand Up To Cancer.
Six very different PC games are coming together in one limited-time bundle that spans kaiju-sized brawls, tactical deckbuilding, psychological horror, survival, and relentless boss battles.
Available from October 19 at 12:00 AM PDT through November 2 at 11:59 PM PST, the gamescom asia bundle includes Steam keys for GigaBash, HELLCARD, Gordian Quest, Winion Virus, Monstrum, and UNYIELDER. The complete collection costs $9.99 USD through a single checkout.
The six games have a combined regular price of $123.94, making the bundle 91% off. The combined value is based on standard U.S. Steam regular prices as of October 1, 2026.
The promotion also supports an important cause, because 10% of the bundle purchase price (less all applicable taxes, fees, and refunds) goes to Stand Up To Cancer. Restrictions apply.
Here's some more info on each game included in the bundle:
GigaBash
Developed by Passion Republic Games, GigaBash is an arena brawler in which up to four players control towering kaiju and giant heroes. Players can throw opponents, unleash enormous attacks, and flatten destructible cities in battles inspired by classic monster movies and couch-friendly fighting games.
HELLCARD
Developed by Thing Trunk and published by Skystone Games, HELLCARD is a cooperative roguelike deckbuilder set inside the paper-crafted dungeons of the Book of Demons universe. Enemy positioning matters alongside card selection, encouraging up to three players to combine their decks and coordinate strategies against increasingly dangerous encounters.
Gordian Quest
Mixed Realms’ Gordian Quest combines old-school role-playing, deckbuilding, roguelite progression, and tactical turn-based combat. Players build a party of up to three heroes, develop their skills and equipment, and discover powerful card combinations across its campaign and replayable challenge modes.
Winion Virus
Dawntown Studio’s Winion Virus is a pixel-art psychological horror visual novel centered on an illegal virtual-pet program called Raising Winions. Its colorful computer interface gradually gives way to a dark, twist-filled story told through dialogue, point-and-click interactions, and immersive 3D sequences.
Monstrum
Monstrum, developed by Team Junkfish, strands players aboard a derelict cargo ship where they must scavenge supplies, evade an AI-driven predator, and find a way to escape. Procedurally generated layouts, different monsters, and permadeath ensure that every attempt presents new dangers.
UNYIELDER
Developed by TrueWorld Studios and published by Shueisha Games, UNYIELDER is an intense movement FPS built around back-to-back boss encounters. Players assemble an arsenal, combine weapons and abilities, and battle through a gauntlet of enemies before constructing and confronting their own final boss.
Purchasers will receive their individual Steam keys by email immediately after completing checkout. The gamescom asia bundle is available for $9.99 only from October 19 through November 2, so visit the campaign page before the promotion ends to pick up all six games and support Stand Up To Cancer.

Staff on the D&D and Studio X teams will now vote in a National Labor Relations Board election
Wizards of the Coast is refusing to grant voluntary recognition to a union drive by its Dungeons & Dragons and Studio X teams. Staff will instead vote on joining in a secret-ballot election overseen by the National Labor Relations Board.
According to Wargamer, the union, United Wizards of the Coast-CWA, announced the decision on Twitter/X on Wednesday, October 14, and a company spokesperson confirmed it.
Wargamer obtained an email apparently sent to Wizards' US staff, in which the company says it is "not neutral on the question of unionization." It adds that it prefers to deal with staff directly rather than through unions.
The email says eligible employees have the right to decide for themselves, and that Wizards will honor the outcome of the election whichever way they vote.
It also lists subsidized medical benefits, five weeks of paid time off, annual bonuses at 200% of target in 2025, and a 20% rise in individual contributors' average base salary since 2023.
Staff on both teams said they intend to unionize on October 6 and asked the company to recognize the union by October 13.
The union's stated aims include fair pay, promotion routes and job security, remote work protections, and better healthcare.
The union is calling for an enforceable AI policy. In the petition it published when the D&D and Studio X teams announced their drive, workers said leadership had pushed for generative AI without regard for their teams' wishes.
It is also seeking ownership of what employees create in their own time, a demand it first made when the Arena team announced its union in April. Wizards and Hasbro missed the deadline to voluntarily recognize that union in May.
United Wizards of the Coast-CWA was formed by the Magic: The Gathering Arena team, which voted to unionize in June by 79 votes to 16.
Wizards of the Coast is part of Hasbro, whose second-quarter results show its Wizards of the Coast and Digital Gaming segment made an operating profit of $567.7 million on revenue of $1.25 billion in the first six months of 2026.
Over the same period, Hasbro's Entertainment segment made an operating profit of $22.9 million, while Consumer Products posted an operating loss of $62.0 million.

news.body:
Brunch Studio Reveals How They Made the Valorant: Through The Cracks Cinematic Trailer
Valorant: Through The Cracks is a trailer reveal for Summit, the new VALORANT map that follows the events of Why We Fight Back.
Brunch Studio
Brunch Studio shared a series of breakdowns of the Valorant: Through the Cracks cinematic trailer presented by Riot Games back in June. The trailer reveals a new VALORANT map – Summit.
Summit is a training facility high up in the mountains of China. There, Sage tries to recover from the injuries following the events of Why We Fight Back. However, the wounds from Viper's relentless attacks take over Sage's body, forcing her to confront the radianite serpent to stop the painful crystallization of her body from spreading further.
The stunning cinematic trailer was directed by Paul-Eugène Dannaud and Benoît de Geyer d'Orth of Turbo Collectif. The team used Maya for sculpting and animation. VFX for the scenes were made with Houdini.
In the trailer, you can see how the core shots of the sequence went from a rough concept sketch to a pre-rendered Maya animation to a mesmerizing final render with glowing emerald crystal materials. Compared to the original sketches, for instance, the final version of the serpent has a wider, more rounded head. Sage herself has more crystal-shaped scales on her skin, compared to what was outlined initially.

The 2027 Game Developers Choice Awards (GDCA) will be accepting submissions from publishers and developers for the first time.
Games released on PC or console between January 1 and December 31, 2026, are eligible. Titles must be submitted to be considered.
GDCA 2027 has no entry fees, and the submission deadline is November 1, 2026.
Previously, the GDCA used a nomination-based voting system through the International Choice Awards Network (ICAN), an invitation-only panel of over 500 creators, developers, and industry members.
Two new award categories have also been introduced: Best Game Launch and Best Gaming Tech.
Winners will be announced at the 2027 GDCA ceremony on Tuesday, March 2 at GDC Festival of Gaming.
Earlier this year, the GDC Festival of Gaming announced additional changes for 2027, including a new Business Hall at Moscone West.
Other updates include three new passes, dedicated options for indie developers and start-ups, and a revised event schedule.
"GDC 2027 is about giving people more choices in how they participate at the show, making the week work better for the way the industry uses GDC today," GDC VP of content strategy Mark DeLoura previously told GamesIndustry.biz.
"The changes are about making the event more accessible, making it easier to make meaningful connections and accomplish what you came to GDC to do."

members.title: 触乐怪话：澳门风云

news.body:
我在澳门蹭吃蹭喝。
很巧，和上周五写怪话的周老师一样，我在国庆最后一天去看了《生化危机：爆发夜》。除去恐怖要素，我觉得是挺黑色幽默的一部片子，有些地方甚至让我联想到“辐射”系列。不过，我今天的怪话并非想要聊这部电影，而是我看电影的地方，澳门。更具体一点，是澳门的娱乐场。
为了看IMAX版，我去的是位于澳门葡京人的英皇剧院。过去经常看盗版电影的朋友，应该对“葡京”这个名字不陌生。“性感荷官在线发牌”广告词就是出自盗版电影里植入的“新葡京”广告。但据说，绝大部分这类非法广告只是借用了葡京的名号，实际上和澳门葡京系娱乐场的关系不大。
而“葡京”品牌是由赌王何鸿燊创立的。光是以葡京为名的娱乐酒店，在澳门就有多家，老葡京、新葡京、上葡京还有葡京人。它们之间的关系，我也搞不清楚。就包括，这次去之前，我以为葡京人会和它附近的威尼斯人、巴黎人以及伦敦人一样，是拥有娱乐场的综合体，但实际上它只是一个干净明亮的商场。
这是我今年第二次去澳门。第一次是春节期间，我带来深圳过节的家里人去澳门旅游。我们当时参观的第一家娱乐场就是新葡京。
第一次进娱乐场，我还有点紧张。尤其看着面露凶光的安保，会情不自禁地脑补一些港片里的画面——去年上映的警匪片《捕风追影》就有在澳门的永利皇宫取景。
进去之后里面非常热闹，几乎每个台子都围着人，可能是因为春节，有不少人来发新年财。听说澳门大多数人对于博彩都很谨慎，但许多人会在春节期间去娱乐场讨个彩头。例如，澳门公务员平时被禁止进入娱乐场，只有初一到初三是例外。
然而如今葡京系在澳门的持照经营的娱乐场里，已经日薄西山。从室内装潢到经营模式，和后来开业的金沙集团的娱乐集群比起来，葡京系酒店看上去都要逊色不少。
2007年开业威尼斯人酒店，是拉斯维加斯的金沙集团把他们的成功案例在澳门完成的一次复刻，由于太成功，他们后续又开设了巴黎人和伦敦人。威尼斯人酒店可以说是极尽奢华，商场内人造运河，运河上方是人造天空，永远都呈现出一幅白天的景象，游客也可以花钱乘坐贡多拉，体验“威尼斯”的水上之旅。酒店的穹顶上画着文艺复兴风格壁画，每次看到，我都很好奇，这究竟是贴的壁纸，还是请人画上去的。
于是，这次去澳门我们时间有限，就直接跳过了新葡京，从口岸直接坐上了去威尼斯人的发财车——是的，大家把娱乐场提供的免费接驳车称为发财车。
我们这次去娱乐场除了参观外，还有一个很重要的目标是“蹭吃蹭喝”。之前就有听说澳门娱乐场会免费提供饮料和食物供顾客取用，我上次去却没有见到，也许是太紧张，没注意。但也有人说，因为业绩下降，娱乐场提供的免费食物变少了。有一些更高级的面包蛋糕或者饮品，需要当日消费积分之后，才能领取。
这次逛的时候，我注意到每个娱乐场都确实有设置分发小吃和饮品的吧台，但卖相不如社媒上刷到的那么好看。一开始我还有点不好意思，后来就熟练了，什么豆沙饼、肉松包、橙汁、珍珠奶茶，来着不拒。不过很奇怪，忘了是在哪家娱乐场领到的肉松包，是辣的，而且非常辣，谁会喜欢吃啊。难道是专门整蛊我们这些来白嫖的游客？
可能由于是国庆最后一天，娱乐场里的人不算多，每家逛下来都有不少台子都是空闲的。我发现许多玩客喜欢扎堆，或许是有玄学在其中，比如每个台子有不同的运气。和小时候去过的四川麻将馆相比，澳门娱乐场算得上安静，某次大胜的欢呼声隔很远都能听见。还包括一些私下的低语，娱乐场里会有一些不知道什么身份的人，会悄悄靠近，然后小声问：“换钱吗？”
我其实看不太懂这些博彩游戏的玩法，相比起来，观察玩客的表情会更有意思，也更残酷。为了尊重大家的隐私，我就不展开描述了。
我这次去才注意到，这些玩法下注的金额比我想象得要高很多，大部分的台子下注的最低额度是在300到3000元之间，其中500和1000的最多。也就是说，看上去一位玩客只是损失了一个筹码，但实际上是几百或者上千块。而多数时候，这些玩客为了提升自己的中奖概率，往往会分开押注多个选择，一次性的投入就是几千上万。这还是在普通场，娱乐场中还有一些单独划分开的高消费区域，我从门口过都没好意思走进去。
这大概也是为什么，玩客们的表情都非常严肃——只有我和朋友在里面一路嘻嘻哈哈，显得格格不入。
也有门槛很低的项目，老虎机，下注金额从10块到100块不等。一个很有趣的现象是，有不少老人喜欢玩老虎机，他们会一次充个几百块进去，然后开始不停地按下按钮。
我作为一个抽卡二游的玩家，对于老虎机的运行方式有种莫名地熟悉感。甚至，澳门娱乐场的老虎机也有“出金动画”，会有不同颜色的龙腾飞起来。在播这个动画的时候，我看见老虎机面前的那位奶奶，还随着节奏在高兴地摇摆。
这样一想，我认为自己一定不能碰任何博彩。因为就在上周刚开的《明日方舟：终末地》卡池，我第一个保底歪了，当时给自己立下规矩，说要过两周冷静之后，考虑考虑再抽。但当天上线，根本没忍住，直接梭哈。所以，像我这样的自制力，最多只能去娱乐场当一个蹭吃蹭喝的白嫖游客了。
最后也严肃提醒各位读者，博彩有风险，博彩游戏的长期期望对玩家不利，不应把它当作投资或稳定获利方式。

members.title: 富贵险中求，这些新游准备与《GTA6》头碰头

news.body:
谁能在《GTA6》的流量海啸中分得一杯羹？
种种迹象表明，《GTA6》几乎肯定会成为历史上首发销量最高、玩家规模最大的游戏。
8月底，《GTA6》加长版预告片在流媒体平台Netflix上线，随后在短短4天内就积累了超过3100万次观看。Sensor Tower的追踪数据显示，截至目前，这款开放世界动作游戏的预购量已超过575万份，且大多数预购玩家都选择了售价100美元的终极版。据该机构估算，尽管距离正式发售还有1个多月，《GTA6》已经创造了超过5.6亿美元的收入。
考虑到《GTA6》对玩家的巨大吸引力，许多主流发行商纷纷避其锋芒，做出延期推出新作的决定。例如，微软Xbox将《神鬼寓言4》的发售档期从今年第三季度推迟至2027年2月，Cloud Imperium也为了避免“与关注度空前的《GTA6》撞车”，将此前已数次跳票的《星际公民》单人战役衍生作《42中队》推迟到明年发布。
不过，也有几家公司选择与《GTA6》同期发布游戏，策略游戏《火焰、森林与洪水》（Flame, Forest and Flood）的开发商Fairy Mount就是其中之一。
“我们决定在11月19日推出新作，这本身就表达了一种态度。”工作室首席执行官布拉泽·兹维奇兹尼斯基（Blazej Zywiczynski）说，“与《芭比》和《奥本海默》同天上映的情况类似，我们的游戏虽然与《GTA6》同时发布，但两者的玩法和风格截然不同。《GTA6》依托于一个拥有数十年历史、根基深厚，吸引了无数热情粉丝的知名系列，《火焰、森林与洪水》则是一款由经验丰富的开发者倾注心血打造的全新游戏。”
兹维奇兹尼斯基将《火焰、森林与洪水》描述为“一款适合全年龄段玩家和非玩家的多人策略游戏”，并声称该作拥有“GTA”系列所不具备的特质。“事实上，我们引入了人们从未在电子游戏里见过的一些全新玩法。《火焰、森林与洪水》不会让玩家对着老奶奶的脸开枪，但它是一款玩家可以和奶奶一起玩的游戏。总之，两部作品面向完全不同的受众群体，登陆不同平台，美术风格和情感基调也大相径庭。”
按照兹维奇兹尼斯基的说法，通过在《GTA6》发售当天推出《火焰、森林与洪水》，他还希望“为小型游戏开发团队表明立场”。“如果坊间传闻属实，《GTA6》的预算远超10亿美元，那么这个数字相当于我的游戏研发预算的4万倍，但我们丝毫不感到畏惧。”他说，“我们凭什么要把整个11月拱手让给一款规模极度膨胀的偷车模拟游戏？”
与《火焰、森林与洪水》一样，2D像素风动作冒险游戏《沃尔维冒险：重制版》（Volvy's Adventure: Reslimed，暂译）也将与《GTA6》几乎同时发售。该作由独立工作室Doinksoft开发，采用平台过关玩法，以发行商Devolver Digital旗下吉祥物为主角。在Steam商店，一向以擅长整活闻名的D社将其描述为“对那款由史上最著名电子游戏吉祥物担任主演、此前从未正式发行的动作平台游戏的原始重制版的精彩复刻”，而在公司官网的一篇博客文章中，D社更立下豪言壮语，声称它是“11月19日游戏行业最重磅的新品”。
当被问到D社为何决定在11月19日发布《沃尔维冒险：重制版》时，D社品牌策略师罗比·帕特森（Robbie Paterson）反问：“为什么不呢？从公关宣传的角度来看，《GTA6》肯定会抢占绝大多数游戏媒体、主播和玩家的注意力，但它并不首发登陆Steam，所以我们认为，其他新品仍有呼吸的空间。与此同时，我们可以借此机会整活搞怪，让我们那位勇敢无畏的吉祥物，与近十几年来最受瞩目的游戏刚正面！”
“既然我们自信地宣布要在《GTA6》发售的同一天推出新游戏，‘如何脱颖而出’就不是什么问题了。”帕特森补充，“我们非常幸运，Devlover已经积累了足够的声望，所以新品消息能够引起不少玩家关注。在接下来的一个月里，随着《GTA6》进行大规模宣发，我们打算像‘猫鼠游戏’那样灵活借势，让吉祥物沃尔维以各种方式频繁进入玩家视线。当然，我们在Steam平台也将面临竞争，但我希望沃尔维的粉丝们都来支持这位老朋友。”
兹维奇兹尼斯基指出，作为一家知名发行商，D社拥有众多独立游戏开发商所不具备的强大营销实力。在他看来，大多数独立工作室不宜盲目照搬D社的做法，而是应当另辟蹊径，想方设法利用有限的时间和空间，努力向玩家展现自家游戏的亮点。
“《GTA6》确实声势浩大，任何游戏都很难跟它比拼热度，但我们为何要那么做呢？”兹维奇兹尼斯基说，“我的看法是，玩家并不想听到更多的喧嚣声。事实上，我们希望为玩家提供一种远离喧嚣的选择。《火焰、森林与洪水》在方方面面都与《GTA6》截然不同：人们能够从这款PC游戏中获得温馨惬意的体验，既可以独自游玩，也可以与平时不玩游戏的朋友、孩子或情侣一起玩，发挥聪明才智、分享纯粹乐趣，共同度过美好时光。这正是许多人梦寐以求的体验。”
“就算我们真的想搞出点动静，也绝对不会落入俗套。比如，我可能邀请山姆·豪瑟跟我来一场CEO对CEO的K歌对决，地点和歌单由他定。我敢肯定，某些行规将会让这位R星总裁选择避战。”
据兹维奇兹尼斯基透露，Fairy Mount没有为《火焰、森林与洪水》设定具体的销量目标。“考虑到市场竞争的激烈程度，为一款新游戏设定预期销量意义不大。”不过他认为，从经济角度来看，与像《GTA6》这样的3A大作相比，立项开发独立游戏的风险要小得多。
“如果《GTA6》的预算确实达到了传闻中的20亿美元，那么Take-Two必须以100美元的价格卖出超过2850万份游戏，才能实现收支平衡。”兹维奇兹尼斯基解释，“作为比较，《火焰、森林与洪水》的定价低得多，却只需要卖出不到1万份就可以回本……就算本世代主机的所有用户都购买一份《GTA6》，其投资回报率也才勉强达到5倍，而《火焰、森林与洪水》只要卖出大约3万份，就能实现同样的投资回报率。放眼整个市场，究竟有几款3A游戏能保底卖出3000万份？《艾尔登法环》仅仅勉强回本，‘刺客信条’系列则只有极少数几代作品的销量能达到这个数字的一半。”
“还有个值得深思的问题是：玩家为游戏花的钱，究竟去了哪里？如果你掏出100美元购买《GTA6》，那些辛勤工作的一线开发者可能连一分钱都拿不到。你也可以花100美元购买5-10款风格迥异、充满实验性，并且勇于突破常规的游戏，而在这笔钱当中，70%都会直接流向开发者，从而助力他们在未来创作出更多优质游戏。”
D社有没有为《沃尔维冒险：重制版》设立任何销售目标？对于这个问题，帕特森半开玩笑地回应称：“当然，我们希望《沃尔维冒险：重制版》能够超越《GTA5》，成为历史上首发销量最高的电子游戏。但我们得脚踏实地。我们很高兴有机会在《GTA6》问世的同时，推出一款令我们引以为豪的游戏。到目前为止，玩家的反馈让我们倍感欣喜。等等看吧，如果这款新作真的能登顶畅销榜，说不定我们真该为吉祥物沃尔维立雕像了。”
业内分析师普遍认为，对游戏厂商来说，在《GTA6》发售当天推出新品并非明智之举。
“在《GTA6》发售的那一周内，主机平台上的任何其他新游戏或者相关公告，恐怕都很难引起人们的关注。”游戏产业分析机构Aldora首席执行官约斯特·范德鲁南（Joost van Dreunen）直言，“《GTA6》将会制造一个巨大的关注度黑洞。在本就拥挤不堪的游戏市场，如果哪家厂商非要头铁地在那时候发布新品，无异于白白浪费营销资源。”
另一家市场研究机构Ampere Analysis的高级研究经理露易丝·伍德里奇（Louise Wooldridge）则认为，一般来说，游戏厂商确实应当避免在《GTA6》的发售窗口推出新品，但如果产品本身“与《GTA》面向不同的受众群体”，那又另当别论。“《GTA》看似无处不在，甚至跨越了不同媒介，但仍有一部分玩家对它兴趣寥寥，并且很可能永远不会上手游玩。与开放世界动作冒险游戏相比，策略、治愈系或家庭向游戏等相对小众的新品，显然更容易与《GTA6》共存。”
按照伍德里奇的说法，《GTA5》的“绝大部分”玩家平时也玩其他大型动作游戏，例如《堡垒之夜》和《使命召唤》。“据我观察，喜欢叙事向单机游戏的《GTA5》玩家就少多了。”她透露，“因此，尽管《GTA6》发售初期的影响力有望超过《GTA5》，却不太可能对那些在类型、主题、玩法或规模上与它几乎没有任何共同点的游戏造成巨大冲击。换个角度来看，《GTA6》或许还会利用自身热度进一步拓展市场，从而令其他游戏作品受益。”
另一方面，至少在现阶段，《GTA6》的影响力还无法渗透PC平台。“与主机游戏发行商不同，Steam上的发行商们暂时不用承受《GTA6》发售带来的全部冲击。”伍德里奇解释，“在《GTA6》最终登陆该平台前，Steam发行商有机会让自家产品吸引玩家关注，并与玩家建立良性互动。如果你的游戏与《GTA6》风格迥异，能够为玩家提供差异化体验，更应尝试利用像这样的宝贵机会。”
范德鲁南补充：“就玩家整体关注度而言，PC乃至移动端游戏市场或许会受到少许波及，但这些市场与主机游戏市场差异巨大、相对独立，并不会遭受太大冲击……《GTA6》就像一部即将出版的奇幻小说，在奇幻小说爱好者的圈子中备受期待，却不太可能吸引钟爱成功学书籍的读者。”
如果一款新游戏将与《GTA6》同时发布，厂商究竟应该怎样做，才能确保它在激烈的竞争中脱颖而出，吸引玩家的广泛关注？“对于规模较小的团队来说，避开《GTA6》注定会占据主导的那些渠道是明智之举。”范德鲁南说，“小团队应当深耕自有玩家社群，通过这种方式来摆脱外界噪音的干扰。毕竟，他们不可能在火力上压制一家明显拥有更强火力的大厂，那种做法毫无意义。”
伍德里奇提出了更具体的建议。“开发者不可能无视《GTA6》的存在，应当围绕其发售来设计发行策略，而非假装这件事根本不会发生。”伍德里奇指出，“但请记住，你不能将自己的游戏与《GTA6》放在同一纬度上进行比较，而应着重强调它拥有《GTA6》所不具备，或者无法为玩家提供的特质。”
“在产品宣发阶段，你需要聚焦于自家游戏在品类、基调或玩法风格上与《GTA6》的差异，让玩家一眼就能看到其独特性。此外，你还要充分利用平台之间的差异，比如投入更多精力在Steam平台搞营销，提高产品在Steam的曝光度。同样重要的是，你得在11月19日前的几周里就开始积蓄声势……一旦《GTA6》正式发售，任何新游戏都将被它掀起的巨大声浪淹没，因此，开发者务必要利用接下来的这段时间为产品造势，努力推动它激发玩家的兴趣。”
本文编译自：GamesIndustry.biz
原文标题：《"Why should we just give up the entire month of November?" – The indie games going head to head with GTA 6》
原作者：Alex Forbes-Calvin
* 本文系作者投稿，不代表触乐网站观点。

members.title: 自动化机制叠加双视角解谜，《HR.SOS》试玩版亮相Steam新品节

features.body:
自动化与解谜结合的模拟经营游戏《HR.SOS》已正式参与Steam2026年10月新品节。本作由玩家同时扮演CEO与HR，接手一家全面停摆、资金告急的公司，通过重构生产流程与人力分配，逐步将其打造为高效运转的商业帝国。游戏现已发布试玩Demo，玩家可前往Steam平台免费下载体验并加入愿望单。
在玩法设计上，本作将公司的宏观扩张与微观管理深度融合。处于CEO视角时，玩家需要从基础的手动生产与销售做起，随着科技树的解锁与资金积累，将精力转向产业链规划、运输路线连接及贸易扩展，构建自动化运转的商业流水线。切换至HR视角后，管理核心则变为人力资源的精准配置。玩家需要根据员工特性安排岗位，优化文件在各部门间的流转路径，避免流程阻滞。
CEO与HR两套机制并非相互独立，而是构成了互为因果的核心游戏循环。CEO模式下生产的文书能够帮助HR招揽高素质人才，从而降低管理成本；而HR模式下修复瘫痪部门后，CEO则能解锁更高利润的业务板块与新部门。这种玩法间的相互驱动，使自动化构建与解谜优化相辅相成，为传统模拟经营品类带来了极具深度的玩法体验。
如果你正在寻找一款玩法有点特别的经营游戏，不妨去试一试这款游戏。

features.summary_raw: 聚焦游戏关卡生成领域，梳理强化学习、大语言模型相关经典论文精华，结合游戏开发场景分享实践启发与思考。

members.title: 基于RL+LLM的关卡生成探索（一）

features.body:
作者：余田 首发“鱼塘游戏制作工坊”公众号
一、前言
莫慌，本文古法手搓，不含复杂概念和公式，只包含论文精华和个人思考，我家猫说她勉强能看懂。
最近对LLM在游戏侧的应用陷入一些瓶颈，其中包括之前文章提到过的那些痛点：幻觉，黑盒，上下文不足，对实际内容没有感知等，总结为“不够可控”，于是想往强化学习（RL）方向看看，进行了一波文献大学习。
而且我最近有个感觉，大家都在疯狂拿AI做产出（包括我），用自己的专家知识和判断，驱动AI不停前进，反过来说，AI像是在不停汲取使用者，人好像变成了AI的燃料（多开的前额叶撕裂者们肯定知道我在说什么）。所以也想系统学习一波，充充能，目的不是做研究，而是汲取一波新上下文 ，看看有没有启发，不管是对游戏开发还是AI应用。
于是进行了一波基于业务和兴趣的大学习，由于这个领域细分太多了，有目的性的学习效率更高，所以先聚焦到关卡生成这个领域，具体理由可以参考之前AI原生游戏的文章。
同时，充分利用AI，我先开发了一个论文阅读助手，一个带术语速查，论文分类管理，关联论文关系等功能的妙妙小工具，大大提高阅读效率。反正是学的过程中，哪里不舒服，都让AI加功能，AI时代学习效率真的提升好多。我不禁有一种感慨：
当前时代，有一个被AI应用效率提升掩盖的巨大财富，就是AI带来的学习能力提升。
虽说是往RL方向看，但实际当前主流都是混合系统，纯RL思路走向AGI的路线主要是sutton和sliver他们在搞，还挺吸引人的。但不重要，我们还是专注于游戏开发，怎么对做游戏有用怎么来。目前读了80+论文，其中有一些我觉得有帮助的，直接贴目录：
这些论文各领域都有，主要可以分为两大类，第一部分是和RL相关+游戏相关的经典论文，用于了解背景知识，对研究历程有个感知，这部分只提取对游戏开发有启发的精华。第二部分是直接跟关卡生成或PCG相关的论文。
这些论文每篇都很长，笔记也很长，本文先进行一部分论文笔记的精华提取，以及个人思考的分享，不会对原文照本宣科，也不涉及复杂的概念，争取用最直白，最不绕弯子的文字稳稳地接住你。
二、论文启发（第一波）
Dota 2 with Large Scale Deep Reinforcement Learning 2019
OpenAI这篇可谓是RL领域的圣经之一了，简而言之，就是OpenAI 19年开发了一个强化学习系统OpenAI Five，用来挑战dota2，经过训练后，2比0击败了世界冠军队伍OG，并且在随后的公开赛中，对普通玩家胜率99.4%。dota2的复杂程度不用多说，非常牛逼。这篇论文有几个我觉得有意思的点：
作者强调，如果要在真实游戏中训练强 AI，工程大于算法。OpenAI Five用的PPO、GAE、LSTM 都不是全新算法，真正困难的是把环境、观测、动作、奖励、分布式训练、版本管理和评估闭环接起来并让它稳定运行 10 个月。工程基础设施比任何单个算法都重要。
训练过程包含大量设计，例如奖励设计，只有胜负这个奖励过于稀疏，他们尝试了，也能训，但是学习速度巨慢。而加入过程奖励设计，包括击杀，补刀，推塔，获得经验，team spirit（促进团队合作用的）等等，效果质变。但他们也承认，整套奖励设计没有怎么大改过，并不是最优的，突出一个够用。这给我的启发是，游戏设计在训练过程中其实能够发挥非常大的作用，好的设计，能够大大提高训练速度，甚至有时候是可行与否的区别。
自博弈能产生超人策略。它可以超越模仿，发现人类不常用但有效的打法。其中超越人类的有个特征我觉得比较有意思，AI会更愿意消耗资源和长冷却技能，而人类常把这些能力留给“后续也许更好的机会”，这太典了！另外，自博弈不能只跟紧邻的上一版进行对战，否则可能会出现循环克制，导致策略收敛，需要引入历史版本。这点后续自己设计AI评估对战的时候也要注意。
过程中评估策略用了TrueSkill，之前写了文章专门介绍过这个。这篇论文是第一篇看的，所以很多RL的术语都得学，一堆陌生术语里突然冒出一个自己熟悉的，有点感动怎么回事！
AlphaStar Unplugged: Large-Scale Offline Reinforcement Learning 2019
这篇也是经典，是deepmind针对星际争霸2做的强化学习系统，并且是离线强化学习系统，离线是指不给智能体边玩边学，而是只能看人类录像来学。例如上面dota2的就是在线强化学习。这篇论文我最有启发的点是：
如何防止AI训练出来的某个策略被针对，AlphaStar的做法是把目标从战胜自己（自博弈），改为尽量战胜一个集合内的所有对手，然后对这个集合内的对手也进行优化，优化目标是不被某个对手全部击败，这样做对抗训练，一起提升。
这对游戏AI的开发有启发，后续开发对策AI，可以做一个新的标准，就是是否能战胜一个集合的目标，来衡量AI的鲁棒性，这在博弈类策略AI里面非常之关键，因为一个策略强弱与否，不单纯是胜率这么简单，是否容易被反制，被反制后的体验如何，这些隐性指标，之前没有被很好量化。另外PVP游戏中，反过来利用，可以用于防止策略收敛，我们要保证每一个策略，不能战胜集合中的所有对手，并且要保持一个合适的比例。
Emergent Tool Use From Multi-Agent Autocurricula 2020
这篇是OpenAI主导的一个研究，他们搞了一个物理模拟的捉迷藏游戏，让两队智能体自己在里面对抗，一方抓一方躲，训练奖励极简，只有被看到-1，藏好+1这样。环境里有各种工具，比如箱子，斜坡等，但完全不管智能体用不用，只有最终奖励，和两方不停竞争。然后经过大量对局，智能体自发涌现了各种策略，并且是跟人一样的策略军备竞赛，我用更好的策略克制你，你再针对提升策略克制我，如此循环，双方不断变强。这其实就是论文的核心概念：多智能体竞争的自生成训练课程（autocurriculum）。
这个策略军备竞赛过程比较有趣，大体分六个阶段：
双方单纯的追和逃
躲藏者们开始用箱子围住自己，让追逐者进不来，看不到自己
追逐者搬来斜坡攻入箱子堡垒
躲藏者锁住斜坡，不让追逐者用
追逐者利用物理漏洞，踩着箱子滑行
躲藏者锁住箱子
其中比较有意义的是，追逐者涌现了预期之外的物理漏洞利用，并且从实验的角度佐证了我们设计中常用的方法：简单机制+物理就足够涌现出复杂的结果。规则越简单清晰，交互可能性越多，越容易产生涌现的惊喜。
这篇的核心思路其实和前面几篇互相关联，智能体的互相对抗是一种高效的提供挑战压力，促进策略进化的手段，同时可以省去很多过程中的奖励函数设计，奖励设计一直是RL的大痛点，本质上我认为是因为奖励设计本身就代表了设计者对这件事的理解，本质上也是专家知识介入，因此，受限于人类的上限，很难尽善尽美，并且也会限制智能体的上限，只能是一种辅助，一种捷径。
但对于游戏来说，稍有不同，反而是可以吸收自迭代的精华后，更多的用专家知识来控制体验，毕竟游戏的目标不是进化而是体验，就如以前的文章所说，对设计来说，可控涌现才是好涌现。
Human-level performance in first-person multiplayer games with population-based deep reinforcement learning 2018
这篇是多智能体强化学习领域的里程碑成果，专门针对FPS游戏《雷神之锤3：竞技场》的夺旗（CTF）模式进行训练。牛逼的点在于，AI仅以低分辨率的游戏像素画面和游戏得分作为输入，没有为AI行为编写任何人工预设的硬编码规则，训练全程不告诉AI游戏玩法，仅通过最终的胜负结果作为反馈。最终训练完可以对人类胜率达到70%，还能跟人类组队协作。
本篇论文最震撼我的一点是对智能体内部神经网络可解释性的研究，简单来说，作者用一些方法，将智能体的神经元的隐藏状态，转为一张可视化的二维图形，观察到了明显的表征行为，就是对特定场景有规律的激活特定神经元，甚至出现了类似人类“概念神经元”的表现，例如，当智能体的旗帜被夺走时或智能体的队友夺到旗帜时，某个神经元就会被激活。
这真是非常之酷，可解释性正是我当前遇到的最大痛点之一，另外，这个痛点同样横跨神经科学，AI研究，AI应用，复杂系统等领域存在，个人认为，可解释性的研究，是这些领域往上突破且可控的正路。用一句话来说就是：从炼金术变成化学。
Sparse Autoencoders Find Highly Interpretable Features in Language Models 2023
当然，上一篇说的单个神经元相关的，是有局限的。实际的人类神经元和大模型，都是单个神经元会对多个不相关的概念激活，例如同一个神经元既对中国有反应，又对猫有反应，还对冰淇淋有反应。这就是多义性。本质是在能量和空间限制下，有限的大脑认知无限世界，必须要做的压缩，同时，这本身也是是一种高效的做法，大模型也一样如此。这个就是叠加态假设（Superposition Hypothesis）。但这就对可解释性带来了麻烦，就算观察到激活了某个神经元，也不确定它具体代表什么。
本篇的SAE（稀疏自编码器）就是来解决这个问题的。SAE是一个用来搞清楚目标模型在想什么的外挂小模型。我用一个最好理解的例子来解释一下SAE的原理：
第一步，先收集原材料，让原模型读海量文本，在它疯狂运转时，把它内部那些混乱的神经元激活信号数据全部记录下来。
第二步，在原模型外面挂载一个独立的 SAE 小模型。SAE 拥有比原模型多十倍甚至百倍的神经元，并在训练中被死死卡住一个变态规则：“每次只准用最少数最精准的神经元，来还原原始模型的信号”。然后SAE 经过数亿次迭代，逼迫自己用一个神经元代表一个概念，例如42号神经元，只代表某个概念X，在这三句话出现的时候激活。
第三步，自动化贴标签（用AI理解AI）：这时候还不知道42号神经元具体概念X对应是什么，于是，就把这三句话扔给另一个“AI考官（大模型）”去自动分析和总结这些句子的共同点。例如这三句话是：
我有一只猫
有个东西在喵喵叫
大脸猫大脸猫爱吃鱼
经过对比总结，预测，验证等手段，定下42号神经元对应概念是“猫”。其他神经元也同理。
这就是为什么SAE需要比原模型多很多倍的神经元，本质上有点像把原模型高度压缩的概念解压出来，变成一个个单独的概念，自然就好理解了，可解释了。
这里面最重要的一点就是怎么让SAE用最少数的神经元还原原始信号，本论文是最初的L1方法，简单来说就是罚款，SAE训练时每次还原用的神经元越多，信号越强，就罚款越多。这样训出来的虽然能达成目的，但有几个问题：
由于会罚信号强度，即使是正确的神经元，也会倾向把信号强度搞低点，由于强度本身是有意义的，比如非常非常快乐，会被降级成开心，以减少惩罚，因此这里会造成失真，也就是强度收缩（Shrinkage）。
由于会罚数量，因此会有很多本身应该参与表达的神经元，一直不被用到，就会导致这些神经元后续也唤醒不了，这就是死特征（Dead Features）。
虽然惩罚了数量和强度，但实际每个输入到底激活几个神经元，强度如何是不确定的，同时，调参会很敏感，调严格了，压缩过头直接崩坏，调宽松了没意义，而且不同输入，不同规模，情况都会变（全部是单词和全部是长句子的输入，明显惩罚程度需要不一样），所以调参非常麻烦。
Scaling and evaluating sparse autoencoders 2024
这篇就是后续提出的更先进的TopK SAE方法，简单来说，就是不用惩罚的方式训练，而是不管输入是什么，直接指定K个信号最强的神经元。也就是指定你用K个词来描述原始输入。这个方式好处如下：
完全不惩罚每个选中词的强度，因此没有L1方法的强度收缩问题。
模型被迫在每步选 K 个神经元，即使某些神经元不常用，模型也会“翻出来用一用”，大幅减少死特征问题。
只有一个K需要调，而且K不随输入变化，也就是稀疏度一直不变，可以做很多优化，适合大规模计算，适合规模化。
当然也很容易想到，K固定的问题就是不灵活，简单的输入可能浪费，复杂的输入可能不够，后续会有其他更新的方法来优化。
Improving Dictionary Learning with Gated Sparse Autoencoders 2024
这是另一条优化L1方法的路线，也就是gate SAE，原理简单来说就是直接训两个子网络，一个gate网络专门决定要哪些神经元；另一个幅度网络决定每个神经元的强度，两者解耦。好处如下：
两者解耦，互不影响，因此幅度网络完全不会为了压数量而损失强度，彻底解决强度收缩问题。
gate网络自适应数量，不是固定值K，更符合具体输入的需求。
gate网络不会受强度影响，自由选择神经元，也大大减少死特征。
一般情况下，Gate SAE的结果会比topk好，但不是完全上位替代，因为gate复杂度明显要比topk高很多，参数量至少翻倍，并且固定稀疏度K，在很多训练场景下是刚需，因此两种路线算各有优劣。
后续25 26年主流的方法，都是对TopK SAE和gate SAE的改进，大体上的路径
自适应K值，由数据决定
从解释模型到操控模型
从单模态到多模态，从文字到视觉
彻底解决死特征问题
降低大规模训练成本
本质都是基于前面SAE的基本概念，篇幅有限，就先不展开了。
Natural Language Autoencoders Produce Unsupervised Explanations of LLM Activations 2026
这篇是A畜在今年五月提出的另一条道路，用自然语言来直接解释模型，原理也很简单，由两个系统组成，
1激活语义化器 (Activation Verbalizer, AV)：输入模型某层的激活神经元，输出一段自然语言文本，描述它们可能代表什么。
2激活重建器 (Activation Reconstructor, AR)：输入 AV 生成的文本描述，尝试重建出原始的激活神经元。
两个系统通过强化学习（RL） 进行联合训练，目标是最小化原始激活与 AR 重建激活之间的误差。
这个方式的核心优势就是产出是直接的自然语言，人类直接能看懂，并且能描述高层次的认知、推理、怀疑或意图等复杂概念。缺陷就是不像SAE那么精确，并且也会出现幻觉，实验里出现过编造的情况。
NLA和SAE方法不是对立的，各有优劣，两者可以结合起来，有研究者将SAE产出的特征，用NLA来解释，利用了两者的优势，不失为一个好的路子。
三、总结
5k字了，写不完，根本写不完！看一篇，又延伸出好多篇，学不完，根本学不完！感觉大脑褶皱都要学展开了，写作时间有限，本篇先起个头，以强化基础+可解释性这条脉络进行引入，剩下估计还有好多篇，结合实践，慢慢输出吧。
为学日益，为道日损，共勉。

features.rss_content: Hello, Welcome to another Friday. Asteroid damage changes Bilka In 2.0, asteroids dealt damage to space platforms based on the relative speed of the asteroid and the collision would cause the asteroid to slow down. After an asteroid dealt a certain amount of damage, it would simply disappear. It was a bit strange to have the asteroids suddenly disappear into thin air with no indication of when it would happen. As you may have already experienced, version 2.1 reworks this asteroid damage to be dependent on the health of the asteroid instead, combined with asteroids taking damage when they deal damage. However, asteroids no longer slow down as they deal damage to platforms. As you'd expect, an asteroid is destroyed when it loses all its hitpoints by dealing damage. This makes the damage much more predictable, as it is a fixed number per asteroid type, and the remaining damage an asteroid will deal to the platform now directly depends on the asteroid's visible health bar and not an invisible counter of how much damage it already dealt. This means that if you manage to shoot and partially damage an asteroid before you collide with it, it will now deal less damage to the platform. Adjusting the impact We playtested these changes during 2.1 development and immediately noticed a large drawback: medium asteroids would one-shot platforms in orbit around planets like Vulcanus. Before 2.1, the damage asteroids dealt to platforms in orbit would be greatly reduced since the platform isn't moving, but with the new speed-independent algorithm that was no longer the case. To counteract this, we buffed the health and resistances of the space platform hub, so that medium asteroids would no longer kill it in one hit. We decided to hold off on further asteroid damage nerfs, or related changes like buffing platform tile health, until we knew whether this change fixed the issue. During the playtest, several of our platforms fell victim to medium asteroids. After the 2.1 release, we received your feedback that building platforms in Vulcanus orbit was too punishing even after the buff to the hub, so in 2.1.13 we reduced all asteroid damage to stationary platforms by 90%. A medium asteroid could previously do 3200 damage to a platform in orbit; after this change, it was only 320. While this massively reduced the frustration around parked platforms, the damage of medium asteroids was still too high compared to 2.0. Some experiments showed that in 2.0 a medium asteroid would deal around 1700 damage to a platform moving at a relatively slow 160 km/s, while it was 3200 damage in 2.1.13. We wanted to keep some of this increased asteroid damage, but not as much, so with 2.1.21 we reduced the damage of medium asteroids and halved again the damage to stationary platforms, so that a medium asteroid now deals 2000 damage to a moving platform and 100 to a stationary one. This is closer to the approximately 67 damage that a medium asteroid would deal to a stopped platform in 2.0. Additionally, we increased the damage dealt by huge asteroids to also be closer to the 2.0 damage numbers to discourage cheesing the trip to the edge by simply tanking the asteroid damage. So overall, the way asteroids deal damage to platforms is now more predictable by being directly dependent on asteroids' remaining health and independent from their speed. Compared to earlier 2.1 versions, taking a hit on your first few flights or building platforms in dangerous orbits is now less punishing. Space platform acceleration & drag CodeGreen Everyone who has designed and flown a space platform has knowingly or unknowingly experienced the effects of the space platform acceleration expression. This formula is what effectively determines the top speed of a platform, using variables for current speed, thrust, mass, width, and height, though height is unused. The existing formula has served us well for quite some time; however, I've always felt unsatisfied with it. I am but a humble modder of 6 years though, not a dev, so my say in the matter is much smaller in comparison. Upon my request, I was told if I could come up with something better, it would be considered. To improve, we must first identify what to improve, which brings us to the next section: The problem Besides thrust, the biggest influence on the top speed of a space platform by far is its width. It directly scales the drag component of the formula (yes, there's drag in space, deal with it). While being adequate enough to make flying space platforms fun, width has some aspects and implications that I, and many community members according to a poll I posted on reddit a while back, found less than ideal. Thank you to all who voted, and to those who took the time to voice their thoughts and opinions in the comments. ~50% of voters didn't like width, and only ~10% did! The design of a space platform is an intricate process, one that oftentimes involves a sizeable amount of iteration and adjustment. Width is determined by the furthest left/right tiles of the platform, so if one of those adjustments happens to make the platform even one tile wider in one location, the top speed is reduced almost as much as if that whole column of tiles had been filled vertically. This felt unnecessarily punishing, especially since the effect of width on acceleration becomes much stronger the narrower the platform is. That leads to another aspect of width I found odd. Because width is so impactful, it became "optimal" to design platforms with minimal width and maximal height, which I call "pencil ships". Encouraging some shape isn't necessarily bad, since that choice is mostly arbitrary, but I don't think pencil ships are the right shape to encourage. The existence of asteroids already incentivizes narrower designs. There's a natural tradeoff between making a wider platform for more area and the cost of defenses to protect said area. It doesn't make sense to me for the wider ships to also be slower. Because of that, there is virtually no reason to build wider (other than farming for asteroid chunks, I guess), and thus narrow platforms reign supreme. Mp4 playback not supported on your device. A very small "pencil ship" in flight. On a separate note, thrusters are designed around not having any part of the space platform behind them. There wasn't a perfect method to prevent this, so thrusters were made to only prevent building behind them in a finite range. Naturally, some players exploited this behavior, resulting in platforms that have multiple layers of thrusters, AKA "thruster stacking". Since the usual limiting factor to how many thrusters a platform can have is its width, thruster stacking sidesteps this organic restriction entirely. Combined with the aforementioned pencil ship, hyper-unrealistic speeds were achieved with platforms fifty times taller than they were wide. When it comes to balancing, thruster stacking can mostly be ignored, since the majority of players aren't doing it and it wasn't intended in the first place. It does, however, show how absurd narrow platforms can get with the existing formula. Lastly, even if none of what I mentioned above were an issue, the space platform tooltip on the right side of the screen doesn't mention width at all, only speed, mass, thrust, and damage taken. You had no indication that width mattered unless you already knew it did. Obviously, that can easily be solved by adding width to the tooltip, but that wouldn't be necessary if width were to be removed from the acceleration formula and replaced with something else entirely. The solution If not width, then what? There are plenty of interesting ideas for how to balance drag, however only one stuck out to me as the clear winner: Mass. Making drag based on mass addresses everything I mentioned above, and introduces some new and interesting design implications at the same time. For starters, adding tiles to the side of a platform doesn't have as drastic an effect on drag anymore. There's still a downside, as every tile adds up, but it won't be as punishing as before. In fact, it doesn't matter where tiles are added anymore, as they all have the same effect on drag. Shifting the focus away from the shape of the platform and towards the amount of space it takes up encourages clever design, where keeping things compact rewards the effort put in to do so. The idea of doing more with less space also rather conveniently aligns particularly well with quality buildings and modules. If the shape of a platform doesn't have an effect on acceleration, the other aspects of design determine the shape much more than before. Most notably, making ships faster requires a better thrust-to-mass ratio, and the only way to do that is by having more thrusters or higher quality thrusters (or both). A platform twice as wide as it is tall allows fitting twice as many thrusters versus the other way around, so wider ships emergently have the capacity to fly faster, at least with the same amount of mass. The tradeoff between width and defense gains an impactful incentive for actually doing so. Of course, you can still make well-designed narrow ships, or ships of any shape; the point is to expand the design space, not switch what gets punished. The process Hypothesizing a change is one thing, actually implementing it is another. To get a better understanding of what I was dealing with, I plotted the existing formula in Desmos. There were too many independent variables to have a useful graph for testing, so for consistency's sake I decided to make some of them dependent on each other: Mass (or weight as called internally) is scaled using width * height , and thrust is scaled by width / 4 . Now the only variables to control are width and height, with the assumption that the platform uses the entire rectangle of space for tiles, and that the back of the platform has as many thrusters as it can fit. The point where the line crosses the X axis is the top speed of the platform, since that is the speed where 0 acceleration is gained. The acceleration graph for a 50x50 space platform. Now I could start trying out different ways of changing the formula to see how they would affect the graph. From the start, I limited myself to changing only the drag component, since I didn't want the shape of the line itself to change, only how it scales. After a few experiments, I settled on (weight / 200) ^ b in place of width * 0.5 . The 200 comes from the mass of one space platform foundation tile, and b is a magic number between 0 and 1 that depends on how much drag should scale with mass, which ended up being 0.8 at the end. The predecessor mod Simpler Platform Drag did something very similar, with an exponent of 0.5 instead. Of course, making a change this significant cannot be done without extensive testing in game, and I knew my limited selection of space platforms from my own games wasn't going to cut it. Thankfully, I had turned to the reddit community for help in advance, asking for people to send in as many space platform blueprints as they could shortly after the poll. There are too many names to list, but thank you to everyone who sent me blueprints in this post ; I used almost all of them. A good portion of them were more optimized for width, which makes sense, but it's important to see how existing designs will be affected. There was still enough variety between all of them that I had a pretty good idea of how everything was affected overall. I couldn't fit all of them, but these are the beasts that helped shape the future. After much iteration, V453000 and I decided on the numbers together, which gave us the new formula present in 2.1.21. Here's a comparison of old (red) to new (blue) for a space platform 50 tiles tall, with width scaling up to 1000 tiles to see how it behaves as it gets wider. Mp4 playback not supported on your device. As you can see, it starts off slightly slower than the old formula, but as width increases, so does the top speed, with diminishing returns, until it reaches a point where it becomes worse to add more width. This lines up exactly with what we wanted, where building wider rewards the player with a higher speed, but not to the point where the optimal ship is an infinitely long wall. The only ships that were significantly hurt in testing were those making excessive use of the thruster stacking exploit; the rest of the skinnier ships didn't suffer too harshly. The wider ships and the tiny starter ships gained some speed, since they already had a decent thrust-to-mass ratio. With this change, narrow ships no longer have dominating speeds, wider ships don't get punished just for being wide, and designing space platforms should be more fun overall. 2.1 has been in experimental for quite some time now, and since this change retroactively affects all existing platforms, I apologize that this wasn't done earlier in development. I do hope you'll enjoy making more space platforms from this point on, and it'll be exciting to see what cool and unique ships everyone will be making. Many thanks to Wube for accepting the change and having me write this section, it's been a pleasure sharing the journey with you all. Community spotlight - Biter Battles Carl Most of us enjoy Factorio as a peaceful (well, peaceful-ish) game where you build your factory at your own pace. But there are always a few who want a bit of a different challenge, and over the years a competitive scene we never really imagined has grown around the game. Biter Battles (BB) is a scenario originally written by M3wM3w at Comfy Factory back in 2018. Two (or more) teams build their factories side by side, and the goal is to feed science packs to the biters as fast as possible, which sends increasingly large waves of biters at the opposing team. Whoever destroys the other team's base first wins. Over the past 8 years the community has refined the mode a lot, and watching the top players today is genuinely impressive. If you have already launched your rockets and built your megabase, and are looking for a completely different challenge, there are a few ways to get into it: Casual play - The BiterBattles.org server runs 24/7 on the latest stable vanilla version (no Space Age), with no mods or registration needed. Just find it under Multiplayer → Browse public games. All skill levels are welcome. Ranked play - The Biter Battles (BB) League is a continuously running ladder, free and open to everyone. You just need to link your Factorio account on biterbattles.org . Tournaments - The 3 vs 3 BB Cup runs about three times a year and features some of the fastest and most competitive Factorio players in the world. The matches are streamed on Twitch, and the last Summer Cup reached four-digit live viewer counts. If you want to see what high-level play looks like, check out Zaspar & Dalvos commentating a 3 vs 3 balance test for the upcoming Autumn Cup , or AntiElitz's POV of the Summer Cup semi-final . As always, let us know what you think at the usual places.

ai.title: Advancing coding in low‑resource programming languages
ai.summary_raw: Learn how OpenAI is improving ChatGPT across low-resource programming languages, with new evaluations for software engineering, SQLite, and COBOL migration.

members.title: Advancing coding in low‑resource programming languages

ai.body:
Advancing coding in low‑resource programming languages
Our latest model advances bring stronger capabilities for building and migrating software in low-resource programming languages such as COBOL, Fortran, and Visual Basic. These languages have less code and documentation available for models to learn from than languages like Python and JavaScript, yet support critical infrastructure and essential services around the world. COBOL supports(opens in a new window) more than 40% of online banking systems, 80% of in-person credit card transactions and 95% of ATM transactions, while Fortran is used in weather forecasting(opens in a new window) and nuclear reactor safety analysis(opens in a new window). Improving AI’s ability to work in these languages could help teams maintain and modernize the software that essential services depend on.
This work is guided by feedback from developers and enterprise customers who have told us that coding models often struggle with these languages. Maintaining and modernizing this software can be difficult: documentation may be incomplete, original developers may have left the company, and important business rules may only exist in code. Whether teams are fixing bugs or migrating to another language, they need to preserve the behavior their systems depend on.
To measure progress, we developed two evaluations. MultiLangBench tests whether a model can build a SQLite-compatible database engine from scratch across 20 different programming languages. Our COBOL migration evaluation tests whether a model can migrate existing programs to another language while preserving their behavior. Together, they test two complementary skills: building new software and preserving what existing software does.
Our latest models show substantial improvements across both evaluations, delivering much higher accuracy at lower cost.
On MultiLangBench, GPT‑6 Astra achieves an average test pass rate of 87.4% across 20 programming languages, up from 26.8% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, with improvements in every language tested. GPT‑6 Luna also outperforms GPT‑5.6 Sol, reaching 40.3% at approximately 78% lower estimated API cost.
On our COBOL migration evaluation, GPT‑6.1 Sol achieves 86.6% accuracy at low reasoning effort, compared with just 5.4% for GPT‑5.6 Sol, while costing 39% less. At higher reasoning effort, accuracy reaches 97.9%, nearly saturating the evaluation.
Together, these results show that our models are becoming significantly better at working with a wide range of programming languages, while also becoming more cost-efficient.
MultiLangBench asks a model to build a SQLite-compatible database engine in a specified programming language. The model must organize a codebase, manage state, handle errors, and add new features while preserving existing functionality.
To compare implementations across languages, we use database files as a shared interface. The candidate program receives an initial database and a SQL query, then produces a modified database. We use the reference SQLite implementation to check whether the resulting database has the expected contents. This lets us apply the same tests regardless of the language used to build the engine.
We adapted tests from SQLite’s existing test suite to this format. The evaluation measures how much working functionality a model can build over an extended coding session, reporting both test pass rate and API cost.
At maximum reasoning effort, GPT‑6 Astra achieves an average test pass rate of 87.4% across the 20 languages, up from 26.8% for GPT‑5.6 Sol. Improvements extend to every language tested, including COBOL (10.9% to 72.1%), OCaml (25.6% to 85.8%), Fortran (21.4% to 83.5%), and Visual Basic (27.5% to 89.4%). Astra scores above 83% in 19 of the 20 languages, with COBOL remaining the hardest at 72%.
GPT‑6 Luna offers a lower-cost option that also improves on GPT‑5.6 Sol in every language tested. At maximum reasoning effort, it reaches an average test pass rate of 40.3%. Gains include COBOL (10.9% to 17.1%), OCaml (25.6% to 34.1%), Fortran (21.4% to 31.4%), and Visual Basic (27.5% to 41.6%). These improvements come at an estimated average API cost of $0.77 per sample, compared with $3.48 for GPT‑5.6 Sol, approximately 78% lower.
We are releasing the MultiLangBench evaluation setup and test suite on GitHub(opens in a new window), along with results for each language. Developers can inspect what the evaluation tests, review performance in the languages they use, and identify gaps that matter for their own work.
Our second evaluation asks models to migrate COBOL programs to C++, Java, Kotlin, Python, or Rust while preserving what each program does.
Successful migration requires understanding both the program’s business logic and COBOL’s specific language behavior. COBOL programs often process financial transactions and business records, where details such as rounding rules and missing-record handling reflect business requirements. For example, COBOL’s fixed-point arithmetic discards excess decimal digits unless rounding is explicitly requested. A rewrite that rounds those values instead can run without errors while producing different financial results.
To test whether these behaviors are preserved, we evaluate our models on hidden tests that require byte-for-byte parity on observable outputs. A migration is considered successful only if all tests pass. Behavior-preserving capabilities like these are useful for teams maintaining and modernizing older systems, though applying it to production software still requires expert review and testing against the system’s business rules and dependencies.
On this evaluation, GPT‑6.1 Sol achieves 86.6% accuracy at low reasoning effort, compared with GPT‑5.6 Sol’s 5.4% at the same setting at just 61% of the API cost. At higher reasoning effort, accuracy reaches 97.9%, bringing the evaluation close to saturation. These evaluation results demonstrate progress toward more accurate, affordable code migration for teams modernizing the software their businesses depend on.
These evaluations, alongside direct feedback from developers and enterprise customers, help us see where our models are improving and where they still fall short.
Our goal is to help models apply software engineering skills across more languages: understanding unfamiliar repositories, planning changes, using build tools, running tests, and debugging failures.
You can try our latest models through the API on coding tasks in the languages your team uses. Your feedback on what works, where the models struggle, and which languages or workflows we should focus on next helps shape how we train and evaluate models to better support the software you depend on.

My obituary for programming (via) Jeremy Scheff poignantly captures the key loss caused by coding agents for career programmers who enjoyed the puzzle of developing code:
Programming turned into one of the greatest jobs you could imagine. You got paid to work on tricky little logic puzzles. The trickier the puzzle, the more you got paid. But even pretty simple puzzles were worth a lot of money because regular people just couldn't do it! No, they needed us. They would give us a problem and we would solve it the way we wanted. We set the strategy, we made the timeline, we defined what was and was not possible.
If you're a programmer who thrives on building working systems and doesn't care too deeply about the problems solved along the way, LLMs are the gift that keeps on giving.

members.title: AI 开始挑战最复杂的系统：生命

ai.body:
AI 开始挑战最复杂的系统：生命
10 月 17 日，哲源科技发布 WHIRLPO 计算医学平台。
2026 年的 AI 赛道，正在发生一个有意思的转向。当行业目光还聚焦在大模型参数、智能体和通用超级智能上时，扎克伯格把资金押向了一个更棘手的领域：生命系统。
今年 4 月，扎克伯格与妻子普莉希拉・陈创立的 Biohub，启动虚拟生物学计划，投入 5 亿美元搭建配套的数据与实验能力，用来训练能预测生物现象的 AI 模型。到 10 月，这个项目进一步扩大。美国能源部、美国国立卫生研究院和 Biohub 联手，搭建生命预测模型的数据底座，Meta、谷歌 DeepMind、Isomorphic Labs 一同参与。整个项目合计承诺投入 18 亿美元，其中美国能源部未来五年拿出超 5 亿美元，NIH 开放大量已积累的生物医学数据。
这个项目的目标很直接：打造一套可以预测生命行为的 AI，Biohub 称之为虚拟生物学。简单说，就是搭建从分子、基因、细胞，一直到完整生命系统的高保真数字版本。科研人员未来可以像现在提问大模型一样，在电脑里对生命做假设、模拟干预，先完成数字试验，再去实验室做真实实验。
这件事不只是扎克伯格单纯看好生物医药。更深一层看，生命科学正在变成 AI 竞争的第二战场。通用大模型赛道已经烧钱白热化，算力、人才、资本门槛越来越高；而理解生命系统，还是一片没有定型的前沿。谁能让 AI 真正读懂生命，就能建立起比聊天机器人难复制得多的壁垒。
AI 擅长设计分子，但新药研发依旧艰难
AI 和生物医药的结合，并不是新鲜事，也是 AI 最早被寄予产业化期待的方向之一。但十几年走下来，一个核心疑问始终摆在眼前：我们真的离新药更近了吗？
近几年 AI 制药最亮眼的成果，基本都集中在分子层面：蛋白质结构预测、候选分子筛选、分子生成、药物安全性预测、药物靶点相互作用等等。AI 能够一次性产出成千上万候选分子，大幅拓展可供筛选的化学空间，效率提升是实实在在的。
可如果把评判标准从模型跑分，落到一款新药成功上市，现实就没有那么乐观。今年 8 月《Nature Reviews Drug Discovery》发文复盘十多年 AI 制药的发展：虽然各类 AI 算法层出不穷，但真正能产生临床价值的成果依旧有限。很多 AI 药企的项目停留在临床前或者一期、二期临床，进入三期临床的项目很少。
小分子生成方向上，AI 确实更容易找到能和蛋白结合的分子，但这只是配体设计，不等于药物设计。找到一个能绑定靶点的分子，和找到一个在人体内安全有效的药物，完全是两码事。
这也是行业当下最值得反思的地方。过去我们把复杂的生命问题做了简化。AI 擅长回答 “什么分子可以结合这个靶点”，但新药研发真正难的是一连串系统问题：这个靶点为什么会引发疾病？干预靶点之后，人体整套生命系统会产生哪些连锁反应？为什么同一种药，有的人有效，有的人无效？为什么细胞、动物实验效果很好，到人体临床试验就失败？
药物分子不是孤立起效。它进入的是一套动态复杂系统，基因、蛋白、细胞、组织、器官、免疫、代谢，再加上外部环境，所有因素互相影响。药物能不能成功，关键恰恰就在这套系统里。 由此带来一个根本性问题：如果 AI 只能看懂分子，看不懂完整生命系统，那它能把新药研发带到哪一步？
从单点分子模型，走向生命世界模型
这也解释了 2026 年 AI 生命科学的核心变化：建模尺度不再局限于单个蛋白、分子或者细胞，开始向上延伸，构建生命预测模型。目标不再只是预测蛋白结构，而是刻画生命状态，预判系统受到干预后的变化，模拟细胞面对扰动时的反应，也就是业内所说的生命世界模型。
大语言模型学习语言的规律，物理世界模型学习物体运动与空间规则，生命世界模型面对的规则要复杂得多。基因变异改变蛋白表达，蛋白调控信号通路，信号改变细胞状态；细胞之间相互作用形成组织微环境，层层向上影响器官乃至人体。生命本身不是静止的，会生长、衰老、产生代偿、发生突变，还会对外界干预持续反馈。
所以生命世界模型，不是一本静态的生命百科。它的核心是弄懂生命如何运转，预测当某一个变量被改变之后，整个系统后续会如何演变。
一旦这套模型落地，AI 在医药研发里的定位会彻底改变。 旧模式：给定靶点，快速寻找候选分子。 新模式：给定一种疾病，先搞清楚发病根源，再判断该干预哪个位置、哪些患者能从中获益，预判干预带来的全身连锁反应。 同样是 AI 赋能新药，两种模式要解决的问题已经完全不一样。
国内同步布局：计算医学写入国家规划
这场转型不是美国独有，国内 AI 生命科学也在从单点算法，转向系统性疾病建模。
今年 9 月，工信部、发改委等十部门发布《医药工业发展 “十五五” 规划》，计算医学首次和 AI、量子计算、超算并列，纳入医药工业未来五年重点技术方向。 AI、超算提供强大的通用计算能力；而计算医学解决的是，怎么把这些算力对接生命系统，用来解决真实疾病问题。
国内哲源科技就是走这条路线的团队。它没有单纯去训练一个更大的生物大模型，而是围绕疾病本身，整合基因组、细胞特征、疾病机制、患者数据、药物干预信息，搭建多层级计算模型，尝试构建一套可以持续推演、训练、验证的生命世界模型体系。
10 月 17 日，哲源科技发布 WHIRLPO 计算医学平台。它并不是一款独立的生物大模型，而是解决更底层的工程难题：如果生命世界模型是下一代生命科学的基础设施，我们需要一套底座，支撑这类模型的训练和运行。
搭建生命世界模型，难度远超训练大语言模型
生命世界模型的落地难度，很容易被低估。 第一是数据难题。大语言模型有海量互联网文本作为养料，但生命领域没有统一的数据集。基因组、单细胞、空间组学、病理、影像、临床数据来源分散，格式、质量、观测尺度差异巨大。很多高价值数据，还需要专门做实验才能产出。Biohub 投入的 18 亿美元，很大一部分资金就是用来生产生物数据，而不是单纯训练模型。
第二是多尺度建模难题。不存在一个大一统的生命模型。研究 DNA 突变、细胞状态、组织微环境、人体疾病，需要不同模型配合。未来完整的生命世界模型，大概率不是单一巨型模型，而是多模型、知识库、工具协同工作的复合系统。
第三是异构算力工程挑战。模型预训练、组学分析、疾病演化模拟、数字患者推演，计算方式各不相同，需要灵活调度 CPU、GPU 等各类算力资源，会遇到传统大模型很少面对的大型科学计算工程问题。
第四，生命模型必须打通计算世界和真实实验世界。语言模型回答出错，可以直接重新训练；但生命模型给出的靶点假说，必须进入实验室验证，实验结果再反过来修正模型，最终还要接受临床检验，模型结论不能只在电脑里自洽。
WHIRLPO 平台正是瞄准这个痛点：整合异构算力、多组学生命数据、模型矩阵、科研工具、智能 Agent 和实验验证链路，搭建从模型训练、科学计算到湿实验闭环验证的基础设施。简单来讲，哲源不是只做模型，而是为生命世界模型打造生产底座。
AI 生命科学，进入基础设施竞争阶段
2026 年，中美两地出现了行业共振。 美国这边，Biohub 联合能源部、NIH、Meta、DeepMind 一起搭建生命 AI 所需的数据、算力、实验基础设施； 国内这边，计算医学写入十五五医药规划，本土团队开始搭建生命世界模型的工程平台。
两件事看似独立，本质指向同一个判断：AI 生命科学，已经从比拼模型指标，进入基础设施竞争时代。
过去行业比拼的，是谁的蛋白预测更准、谁生成分子效果更好、谁能把某一个研发环节提速。 下一阶段比拼的核心，变成：能不能拿到大规模高质量生命数据；能不能跨越基因、细胞、组织、人体不同尺度建模；能不能把多个模型协同调度；能不能让模型持续和真实实验闭环验证；最终实现 AI 从处理生命数据，升级为理解生命系统。
AI 制药过去十几年，方向并没有错。我们此前攻克的，只是生命问题里相对容易计算的那一部分。 分子固然重要，但药物治疗的对象不是分子，是人。从一个候选分子，到在人体上产生疗效，中间隔着一整套完整复杂的生命系统。
如果生命世界模型成为继语言模型、物理世界模型之后，AI 的下一个核心方向。未来最大的机会，未必属于那些小幅刷新模型指标的团队。 真正稀缺的资产，不是又一个生物 AI 模型，而是一套能够让 AI 走进真实生命世界的完整基础设施。
